tool_input.message:
Review of 954b63c (internal/mcp/poll_tools_test.go): zero findings. Both fixes hold, no assertion weakened, no interval skipped.

(a) Poller leak. Fix is `t.Cleanup(poller.Stop)` at <repo>/internal/mcp/poll_tools_test.go:44, registered inside newMarkerServer AFTER testenv.New (line 33) and testserver.NewFixture (line 34). Go runs t.Cleanup LIFO, so poller.Stop fires first, then the IMAP fixture's listener close (testserver/fixture.go:107), then testenv teardown. Stop (email/poller.go:151-160) closes stopCh and wg.Waits, and startLoop (poller.go:209) does wg.Add(1) under the mutex before the goroutine starts, so Wait cannot race Add. Stop on a never-started poller is a no-op (stopCh nil), so the five tests that call newMarkerServer without set_poll_interval are unaffected. Each subtest in TestSetPollInterval_AcceptsEveryValidInterval (line 260-270) calls newMarkerServer(t) with the subtest's own t, so cleanup is per-subtest, not deferred to the parent. This is equivalent to the setupHandlerWithPoller pattern at handler_test.go:118.

Ran: `go test -race -count=3 -run TestSetPollInterval_AcceptsEveryValidInterval -v ./internal/mcp/` — 3/3 PASS, all 9 subtests (1m 2m 3m 5m 10m 15m 30m 1h 2h) each run, no race report, no "use of closed" output, no leak warnings. Also `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/mcp/ ./internal/email/` ok, and `golangci-lint run ./internal/mcp/` 0 issues.

(b) cronExpr 60-divisor. Line 368: `case d < time.Hour && d%time.Minute == 0 && 60%int(d/time.Minute) == 0`. The `d%time.Minute == 0` guard precedes the division so int(d/time.Minute) is never 0 for d < 1h (d would be 0 only if the map held a zero duration, and require.True(ok) at line 366 plus the map contents at email/config.go:182-192 rule that out). I exercised the switch in a scratch program: every current valid interval maps to its expected shape; 45m, 7m, and 90m all fall through to default, which is t.Fatalf at line 376. The comment (lines 358-362) correctly describes the */45 semantics.

Not weakened: the 60-divisor is a strictly added conjunct, so the only change in behavior is that a non-divisor would now Fatalf instead of emitting a wrong "*/N" row. The switch still covers all 9 entries in validPollIntervals; TestInboxDoc_ListsFullIntervalSet (line 421) still iterates the full set via cronExpr. Commit touches only the one test file, no production code.

---
name: list-every-file-a-criterion-touches
description: Write-set gaps on 2026-10-22 came from criteria that implied a file the write set omitted; before ethos mission create, derive the write set from the criteria, not the other way round
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Twice on 2026-10-22 a worker stopped at a write-set boundary that was my
contract defect, not theirs: m-2026-10-22-014 (making "3m" valid broke two
tests in files I had not listed) and m-2026-10-22-025 (a criterion said "add
a test in cmd/beadle-email" but the write set held only admin_cmd.go, not
admin_cmd_test.go). Each cost a failed close, a successor mission, and a
round of crossed messages.

**Why:** write sets are immutable ([[write-set-cannot-be-amended]]), so an
omission is always a full re-scope. The criteria are where the files come
from; I was writing the write set first and the criteria second.

**How to apply:** after drafting success criteria, walk each one and ask
"which files must change for this to be true?" For any test criterion, the
`_test.go` sibling is in the set. For any value added to a validation set,
grep the tree for the OLD canonical invalid fixture and add those test
files. Only then write the write_set block. Related:
[[judge-workers-by-transcript-not-hook-files]].

---
name: steer-before-submit-or-open-a-new-mission
description: A steer sent to a worker after it submits its result races the close; four times on 2026-10-22 it landed as a post-close commit outside any contract
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-22, four separate times a mid-round steer of mine reached a
worker after it had already submitted its result and I had closed the
mission: the errors.AsType idiom (201a5bc), the PollIntervals export
(5d3beb2), the listedTool dedupe (9c5f0b5), and the LDFLAGS stamp
(e438ec6). Every commit was correct and stayed, but each landed outside any
contract's audit record, and one raced a T4 I had assigned to a second
agent on the same checkout.

**Why:** ethos closes on the submitted result; a steer is only inside the
mission if the worker sees it before `ethos mission result`. Messages and
submissions cross within a minute. "Do not commit after submitting" helps
only if the worker reads it before acting on the steer.

**How to apply:** check `ethos mission results <id>` before sending any
steer. If a result is already in, do not steer; close the mission and put
the change in the next contract or a typed T4 spawn. Tell every worker in
its first brief: a steer that arrives after you submit gets a reply asking
for a new mission, never a commit. Related:
[[list-every-file-a-criterion-touches]], [[resume-agents-never-restart]].

name: provisioning-targets-race-on-shared-bin-dirs
description: beadle's tools-biff and tools-beadle-email (fix/ethos-mcp-serve, 2026-10-22) replace binaries non-atomically in host-global dirs; concurrent make test runs break each other; fix is in orphaned mission m-2026-10-22-032
metadata:
  type: project
---

On branch fix/ethos-mcp-serve (unmerged as of 2026-10-22), `make test`
depends on tools-ethos, tools-biff (uv tool install --force into
`uv tool dir --bin`, ~/.local/bin), and tools-beadle-email (go build -o
into GOINSTALL_BIN, ~/go/bin). strace by the silent-failure reviewer showed
uv unlinks then re-symlinks the biff entrypoint, and go build on a cache
hit removes-then-truncates the destination. I reproduced the race
myself: my scrubbed-PATH demo failed on the biff subtest because the
evaluator's concurrent `make tools-biff` was mid-replacement
(timestamps: test 19:24:20, biff recreated 19:24:42).

The fix (per-checkout `.tmp/bin/` for the self-build; `uv tool list`
gate so tools-biff only reinstalls on a pin change; one TESTING.md
sentence on the single-writer assumption) was folded into mission
m-2026-10-22-032, which was orphaned mid-work when the adb worker died on
the account API usage limit (returns 2026-11-01). Tree was clean; the
contract and addendum are in `.tmp/missions/provision-r2.yaml` and my
message history.

**How to apply:** never run two `make test` invocations on this host at
once while that branch's Makefile is in effect, including an evaluator in
the same worktree. When resuming after 2026-11-01, respawn adb on 032
(or abandon and recreate; it has no result), then the combined
registry-test/harness-discriminator mission drafted at
`.tmp/missions/harness-discriminator.yaml`. Related:
[[nested_worktree_gosec_artifact]].

tool_input.new_string:
# Per-checkout, not host-global: tools-beadle-email self-builds THIS
# checkout's own branch content, so its output directory must not be
# shared with any other checkout. $(CURDIR) (not a bare relative ".tmp/bin")
# because `go test` runs each package's test binary chdir'd into that
# package's own source directory, not the repo root -- a relative PATH
# entry would resolve against the WRONG directory inside the test
# subprocess. Gitignored already (.tmp/* in .gitignore); mkdir -p below
# creates it on demand.
BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN := $(CURDIR)/.tmp/bin

tools-beadle-email: ## Self-build this branch's beadle-email into BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN (same test)
	mkdir -p $(BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN)
	go build -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" -o $(BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN)/beadle-email ./cmd/beadle-email/

# go install places a binary in $GOBIN if set, else $GOPATH/bin -- neither is
# guaranteed to already be on PATH. Without this, `make test` provisions
# ethos successfully but exec.LookPath("ethos") still fails: tools-ethos
# ran, the binary exists, and the remedy message points right back at the
# command that was just run. Computed once, at parse time, so every `test`
# invocation prepends the same directory `go install` actually used.
# This directory IS host-global (shared by every checkout on the host),
# which is safe only because ethos is pinned to the identical
# $(ETHOS_VERSION) everywhere -- two concurrent `go install`s race to
# write the same bytes, not different ones. beadle-email's self-build
# does NOT share this directory (see BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN above): its content
# is per-branch, so two checkouts building concurrently into one shared
# directory would let either one silently run its tests against the
# OTHER checkout's binary. An earlier version of this comment argued for
# "exactly one PATH prefix" across both tools; that argument held only
# while both built into the same host-global directory, and no longer
# applies now that beadle-email has its own per-checkout one.
#
# GOPATH may be a colon-separated list (":"-joined on every GOOS, including
# darwin and linux -- Go never uses the OS path-list separator here). `go
# install` with no GOBIN always writes to the FIRST entry's bin/, so take
# only that entry -- appending /bin to the whole list would name a directory
# nothing was ever installed to, and would also inject a second, wrong
# directory onto PATH.
GOINSTALL_BIN := $(shell go env GOBIN)
ifeq ($(GOINSTALL_BIN),)
GOINSTALL_BIN := $(shell go env GOPATH | cut -d: -f1)/bin
endif

# `uv tool install` places a binary in `uv tool dir --bin` -- on this host
# ~/.local/bin, distinct from GOINSTALL_BIN above -- so biff needs its own
# PATH prefix rather than reusing the Go one. Computed once, at parse time,
# same as GOINSTALL_BIN, so every `test` invocation prepends the directory
# `uv tool install` actually used. tools-biff's own recipe (above) now
# fails loudly before `test` ever constructs this PATH if the directory
# can't be determined, so by the time this is read a non-empty value means
# a real directory; the $(if ...) below is defense in depth so a direct
# `make test` invocation that skipped its prerequisites never inserts an
# empty PATH component (which both the shell and Go's exec.LookPath treat
# as the current directory).
UVTOOL_BIN := $(shell uv tool dir --bin 2>/dev/null)

test: tools-ethos tools-biff tools-beadle-email ## Run tests with race detection
	PATH="$(BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN):$(GOINSTALL_BIN):$(if $(UVTOOL_BIN),$(UVTOOL_BIN):,)$$PATH" go test -race -count=1 ./...

tool_input.new_string:
- **`ethos`, `beadle-email`, and `biff` are required tools**, each
  installed automatically by a `test`-dependency target — a developer
  never runs any of them by hand except implicitly, the first time
  `make test`/`make check` provisions them.
  `internal/daemon/templates_test.go`'s
  `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal` is the consumer: it runs
  every stdio MCP registry entry's configured command with `--help` and
  fails loudly, per the no-`t.Skip` rule above, if the binary is missing.
  `ethos` is pinned via `Makefile`'s `ETHOS_VERSION` and installed by
  `tools-ethos` (`go install`, into the host-global `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`
  — safe to share across checkouts because the pin makes every concurrent
  install write the same bytes); `biff` is pinned via `BIFF_VERSION` and
  installed by `tools-biff` (`uv tool install`, into the host-global uv
  tool bin dir, `uv tool dir --bin`, for the same reason — and only when
  the pinned version is not already present, so a repeat `make test` on
  an already-provisioned host installs nothing).  `beadle-email` has no
  version pin and is **not** installed into either shared directory —
  `tools-beadle-email` self-builds this branch's own `./cmd/beadle-email`
  with `go build -o` into `$(CURDIR)/.tmp/bin`, a directory scoped to
  *this checkout*, so the binary under test is always the code under
  review in the current branch or worktree, never a prior release and
  never another checkout's in-flight build. The "runs identically" claim
  above holds through `make test` (or `make check`) only: a bare `go test
  ./...` has no `.tmp/bin` on `PATH` and resolves whatever `beadle-email`
  is first on the shell's own `PATH` instead — a prior release, a stale
  build from another branch, or nothing at all. CI installs the same
  three tools via the same targets before its `Test` step and adds the
  per-checkout `.tmp/bin` (an absolute path built from
  `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`), `$(go env GOPATH)/bin` (where `go install` places
  `ethos`), and the uv tool bin directory (where `uv tool install` places
  `biff`) to `$GITHUB_PATH` so `exec.LookPath` finds all three. Because
  `tools-ethos` and `tools-biff` still write to host-global directories, a
  version-pin bump racing against a concurrent `make test` on the same
  host (e.g. two worktrees provisioning at once) can still interleave;
  `tools-beadle-email`'s per-checkout directory is immune to this by
  construction, since nothing else on the host ever writes there.

cd <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
chore(make): close provisioning silent-failure gaps and the host-global race

UVTOOL_BIN := $(shell uv tool dir --bin 2>/dev/null) went silently empty
when uv predates --bin, reproducing the exact failure the GOINSTALL_BIN
prefix exists to prevent: PATH="$GOINSTALL_BIN::$PATH" with an empty
component resolves to cwd, so the remedy text points right back at the
command just run. tools-biff now fails loudly with an install hint when
uv is absent, and with an upgrade hint when `uv tool dir --bin` produces
nothing; the test recipe's PATH never inserts an empty UVTOOL_BIN segment
(the directory is omitted, not spliced in as "").

tools-biff is also now idempotent: it checks `uv tool list` for the
pinned version first and skips the install when already present, so
--force's unlink-then-link window only opens on an actual version bump,
not on every `make test`.

tools-beadle-email's self-build no longer shares GOINSTALL_BIN with
`go install ethos`. That shared, host-global directory was safe for two
concurrent `go install`s of the SAME pinned ethos version (both write
identical bytes) but not for two checkouts self-building DIFFERENT
branch content under the same filename: two concurrent `make test` runs
on one host could silently test one checkout's beadle-email binary
against the other's test suite. tools-beadle-email now builds into
$(CURDIR)/.tmp/bin, a directory scoped to the checkout running the
build; GOINSTALL_BIN keeps its original job (ethos only).

beadle-f34m
EOF
)"

tool_input.message:
Provisioning round 2 re-review done: all five earlier findings and the race fix close their gaps; three residual findings, none critical. No edits made.

Answers to your questions:
- `grep -qx "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)"` is exact: -x anchors the whole line, so v1.19.01 does not match. On this host `uv tool list` prints exactly `punt-biff v1.19.0`. Nit: dots are regex wildcards; `-Fx` would be literal. No real input exploits it.
- If `uv tool list` fails, status is grep's, no match, else-branch runs `uv tool install --force` (pre-fix behavior). Not silent breakage, but the 2>/dev/null hides why and the race guard is bypassed without trace (finding 1).
- `$(if ...)` with UVTOOL_BIN set but dir missing: correct. Nonexistent PATH dirs are skipped by sh and exec.LookPath; no empty component; test fails with accurate `make tools-biff` remedy.
- `$(CURDIR)` under `make -C`: correct, CURDIR is set after -C processing. CI run steps default cwd to $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, so Makefile `.tmp/bin` and workflow line 46 name the same dir. `.tmp/*` gitignored at .gitignore:62.
- UVTOOL_BIN used at Makefile:131 before its `:=` at :192: fine, recipe text expands at run time after full parse.
- SC2129 group at test.yml:45-49 appends all three lines; step shell is bash -eo pipefail so a failing `uv tool dir --bin` aborts loudly. Unchanged pre-existing soft spot: `$(go env GOPATH)` failing still appends `/bin`, impossible after setup-go, not filed.
- Every new recipe line has an error path: 130/131 exit 1; the if at 132-136 takes the status of its last command so a failing install fails the recipe; 149/150 fail on mkdir/go build.

Findings (all in <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve/Makefile):
1. MEDIUM, Makefile:131. Message says "uv too old to support --bin; upgrade uv" whenever UVTOOL_BIN is empty, but the only evidence is the suppressed `$(shell uv tool dir --bin 2>/dev/null)` at :192, which is also empty when HOME is unset, UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR/XDG_BIN_HOME is malformed, or uv config fails to parse. Current-uv developers get told to upgrade in vain. Fix: in the failure branch re-run `uv tool dir --bin` unsuppressed before exit 1 so the real error prints. Same 2>/dev/null at :132 hides why `uv tool list` failed when the idempotency (race) guard silently falls through to reinstall; drop the redirect or print a note in the else branch when list itself returned non-zero.
2. MEDIUM, Makefile:132. Skip check tests a proxy (uv's env list) not what TestMCPRegistry needs (an executable biff on PATH). If the env is at the pin but $(UVTOOL_BIN)/biff is missing (manual rm while tidying, or entrypoint never linked because a foreign biff blocked it, the exact case the --force comment at :124-128 describes), the test fails, remedy at internal/daemon/templates_test.go:224 says `make tools-biff`, and tools-biff prints "already installed, skipping". Remedy cannot remedy. Not reproduced live (would mean deleting a working binary). Fix: `if test -x "$(UVTOOL_BIN)/biff" && uv tool list 2>/dev/null | grep -qFx "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)"; then`.
3. LOW, Makefile:130-131. Diagnostics echo to stdout; the LaTeX recipe at :110/:113 uses >&2. Add >&2 to both.

Observations, not findings: an editable/path-installed punt-biff at 1.19.0 also satisfies the skip, so a developer's local biff checkout is preserved (consistent with the earlier don't-clobber finding; worth a clause in the :124-128 comment). CI composes PATH by hand at test.yml:45-49 instead of `make test`; if BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN ever moves, CI keeps .tmp/bin and fails with a remedy naming a target CI just ran. TESTING.md now states the "runs identically through make test only" caveat correctly, closing the fifth earlier finding.

# --force overrides any `biff` binary already in the uv tool bin dir that
# uv did not install itself (e.g. a distro package or a manual copy); the
# ==$(BIFF_VERSION) pin above, combined with the skip check in the recipe,
# is what actually drives a reinstall on version drift -- --force covering
# an unrelated existing install is the rare case it guards against. An
# editable or path-installed punt-biff at the pinned version also
# satisfies the skip check below (uv's env listing names the version
# regardless of install source), so a developer's own editable checkout
# of biff, pinned to this version, is left alone rather than clobbered.
tools-biff: ## Install the pinned biff CLI if missing, unreachable, or out of pin (needed by internal/daemon's MCP registry test)
	@command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "tools-biff: uv not found on PATH -- install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to provision biff" >&2; exit 1; }
	@test -n "$(UVTOOL_BIN)" || { echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool dir --bin' produced no output; the suppressed probe's real error is:" >&2; uv tool dir --bin >&2; echo "tools-biff: if the message above is empty too, check HOME and any UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR override" >&2; exit 1; }
	@if test -x "$(UVTOOL_BIN)/biff" && uv tool list 2>/dev/null | grep -qFx "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)"; then \
		echo "tools-biff: punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION) already installed, skipping" >&2; \
	else \
		uv tool list >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool list' failed; reinstalling anyway" >&2; \
		uv tool install --force punt-biff==$(BIFF_VERSION); \
	fi

tool_input.message:
Round 3 re-review of 717f046 (Makefile tools-biff): all three residuals are closed; one MEDIUM and one LOW remain, both on wording/diagnostics, no new silent path.

Answers to your five questions, file is <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve/Makefile:

1. `test -x` on a dangling symlink (line 136). Returns FALSE. Confirmed empirically in a .tmp scratch dir: `test -x` follows the link, the target does not exist, exit 1; `-e` also false, `-L` true. So a dangling `biff` link falls to the else branch and `uv tool install --force` relinks it. Gap closed.

2. UVTOOL_BIN-empty branch (line 135). The retry of `uv tool dir --bin >&2` is followed unconditionally by `exit 1`, so the recipe never proceeds with an empty bin dir; it is fail-closed. BUT if the retry succeeds (transient first failure), the developer sees the path printed under the header "the suppressed probe's real error is:" and then the "if the message above is empty too, check HOME..." hint, then exit 1. That is a misleading message: a valid path labelled as an error, with a remedy that does not apply. MEDIUM. Recommend capturing the retry and branching: `out=$$(uv tool dir --bin 2>&1); if test -n "$$out" && uv tool dir --bin >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "tools-biff: the probe succeeded on retry ($$out); the parse-time probe failed transiently -- re-run make" >&2; else echo "...real error is:" >&2; echo "$$out" >&2; echo "...check HOME..." >&2; fi; exit 1`. Still exit 1 (UVTOOL_BIN was captured empty at parse time via `:=` on line 197, so the rest of the recipe cannot be trusted), but the text now tells the truth. Note: `$(UVTOOL_BIN)` is defined at line 197, after the recipe at 133, which is fine because recipe text is expanded at execution time, not parse time.

3. Fall-through note (line 139). Prints on non-zero `uv tool list` ONLY. Confirmed: against an empty isolated UV_TOOL_DIR, `uv tool list` prints "No tools installed" and exits 0, so an empty list does not trigger the note. LOW observation: the else branch is reached by three causes (entrypoint missing/not executable; version mismatch in the listing; list failed) and only the third prints why. The install itself is loud, so this is not silent, but a one-line "entrypoint missing" vs "version drift" reason would make the reinstall self-explaining. Optional.

4. Single shell. Lines 136-141 are one logical recipe line: `cat -A` shows every line ends in `\$` except the final `fi$`. The `@` on 136 covers the whole if/else. `$(UVTOOL_BIN)` and `$(BIFF_VERSION)` are make variables expanded before the shell starts, so shared shell state is not even required. Lines 134 and 135 are separate shells and each is self-contained with its own `exit 1`.

5. Lines without an error path. Line 139 `uv tool list >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo ... >&2` always succeeds by design (the note is informational). Line 140 `uv tool install --force punt-biff==$(BIFF_VERSION)` is the last command of the else branch, so the if/else compound returns its exit status and make stops on failure. Line 135's retry is inside a `{ }` block that ends in `exit 1` regardless. The `-F` on grep (line 136) is strictly tighter than before (dots now literal), so it cannot produce a false skip. No new line can fail without make stopping.

Did not run tools-biff; did not touch host uv dirs (all probes used UV_TOOL_DIR/UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR under .tmp, since removed); did not edit files.

name: recurrence-on-a-recipe-means-restructure
description: When review rounds keep finding new defects in the same shell recipe, stop patching messages and restructure it into enumerable checks with an outcome table
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-22 the beadle `tools-biff` Makefile recipe went through four
review rounds (missions 032, 037, 038, and the residuals after each).
Every round fixed the previous round's diagnostics and the silent-failure
reviewer found a narrower one in the fix: suppressed probe, then wrong
"upgrade uv" hint, then a valid path printed under an error header, then a
stderr-only exit-0 probe misclassified as success. Each fix was correct
and each opened the next gap.

**Why:** the org's recurrence trigger (same class of defect across two or
more fix/review rounds: stop empirical rounds and formalize) applies to a
guard sequence as much as to a state machine. A model check buys nothing
for a shell recipe, but the same move in shell is to make the outcomes
enumerable: fixed named checks, one failure mode each, a comment table of
every (check, condition, message, exit) row, so review becomes "does each
row hold" instead of open-ended reading that always finds one more case.

**How to apply:** after the second review round on one recipe or helper
reports a new defect of the same class, write the next contract as a
restructure with a required shape and an outcome table, not as another
fix list. Brief the evaluator to verify rows. Related:
[[list-every-file-a-criterion-touches]],
[[provisioning-targets-race-on-shared-bin-dirs]].

tool_input.new_string:
# --force overrides any `biff` binary already in the uv tool bin dir that
# uv did not install itself (e.g. a distro package or a manual copy); the
# ==$(BIFF_VERSION) pin above, combined with the skip check in the recipe,
# is what actually drives a reinstall on version drift -- --force covering
# an unrelated existing install is the rare case it guards against. An
# editable or path-installed punt-biff at the pinned version also
# satisfies the skip check below (uv's env listing names the version
# regardless of install source), so a developer's own editable checkout
# of biff, pinned to this version, is left alone rather than clobbered.
#
# Outcome table -- every path this recipe can take. Review this table,
# not the shell: each row is independent and mutually exclusive, and the
# recipe body implements exactly these rows and no others.
#
# | # | Check           | Condition                                     | Message (stderr)                                                    | Exit          |
# |---|-----------------|------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
# | 1 | uv on PATH      | `command -v uv` fails                          | "uv not found on PATH -- install uv (...) to provision biff"         | 1             |
# | 2 | bin dir known   | `uv tool dir --bin` exits nonzero, OR exits 0   | "'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit N): <captured stderr>"             | 1             |
# |   |                 | with empty stdout                               |                                                                        |               |
# | 2 | bin dir known   | exits 0 with non-empty stdout                   | (none -- that stdout becomes the bin dir for checks 3-4 below)       | continues     |
# | 3 | skip decision   | entrypoint executable AND `uv tool list` shows  | "punt-biff vX already installed, skipping"                           | 0             |
# |   |                 | exactly the pin                                 |                                                                        |               |
# | 4a| reinstall reason| `uv tool list` exits nonzero                    | "'uv tool list' failed (exit N): <captured output> -- reinstalling"  | install's own |
# | 4b| reinstall reason| list exits 0 but listed version != pin          | "installed <version|<none>> differs from pin <pin>; reinstalling"    | install's own |
# | 4c| reinstall reason| list exits 0, pin IS listed, entrypoint missing | "biff entrypoint missing or not executable at <path> (pin <pin> is   | install's own |
# |   |                 | or not executable                               | listed); reinstalling"                                               |               |
# | 5 | install         | reached after any of 4a/4b/4c                   | `uv tool install`'s own output                                        | install's own |
#
# No `2>/dev/null` anywhere below: every uv call's stderr is either shown
# (check 2's failure) or captured into a variable the reinstall-reason
# messages can quote (check 4's `uv tool list`), never discarded. Check 2
# runs `uv tool dir --bin` fresh at recipe time rather than trusting the
# parse-time $(UVTOOL_BIN) variable below, which can be stale or wrong
# for reasons the parse-time computation can't diagnose (a transient
# failure at `make` startup, a later export of UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR); a
# transient failure that now succeeds at recipe time simply proceeds --
# there is nothing left to tell the developer to re-run.
tools-biff: ## Install the pinned biff CLI if missing, unreachable, or out of pin (needed by internal/daemon's MCP registry test)
	@command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "tools-biff: uv not found on PATH -- install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to provision biff" >&2; exit 1; }; \
	err=$$(mktemp); trap 'rm -f "$$err"' EXIT; \
	bin=$$(uv tool dir --bin 2>"$$err"); bin_status=$$?; \
	if [ $$bin_status -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$$bin" ]; then \
		echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit $$bin_status):" >&2; \
		cat "$$err" >&2; \
		exit 1; \
	fi; \
	listing=$$(uv tool list 2>&1); list_status=$$?; \
	if [ $$list_status -eq 0 ] && test -x "$$bin/biff" && printf '%s\n' "$$listing" | grep -qFx "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)"; then \
		echo "tools-biff: punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION) already installed, skipping" >&2; \
	else \
		if [ $$list_status -ne 0 ]; then \
			echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool list' failed (exit $$list_status): $$listing -- reinstalling anyway" >&2; \
		else \
			installed=$$(printf '%s\n' "$$listing" | grep -F 'punt-biff ' | head -1); \
			if [ "$$installed" != "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)" ]; then \
				echo "tools-biff: installed $${installed:-<none>} differs from pin punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION); reinstalling" >&2; \
			else \
				echo "tools-biff: biff entrypoint missing or not executable at $$bin/biff (pin punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION) is listed); reinstalling" >&2; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		uv tool install --force punt-biff==$(BIFF_VERSION); \
	fi

chore(make): restructure tools-biff into enumerable checks with an outcome table

Four rounds of fixing tools-biff's diagnostics each closed one finding
and opened a narrower one on the same lines: merging stderr into a
retry capture misclassified a stderr-only exit-0 probe as success, and
a 2>/dev/null on the list capture hid why the list failed. The pattern
was the approach, not the wording -- diagnostics built from stdout and
stderr merged or discarded ad hoc have no way to express "succeeded with

- The EXIT trap fires on `exit 1` inside a `{ }` group and inside an `if` branch. Trap is set on line 163 before the first path that needs it (line 167). Check 1's `exit 1` on line 162 runs before mktemp, so there is nothing to clean there.
- Separate capture does not lose the stdout-plus-nonzero case: `bin` keeps the path and `bin_status` keeps the status, and the code classifies it as a row-2 failure, matching the table. The message does discard the captured stdout in that case, which is a small diagnostic loss but inside the table's row.
- `$(UVTOOL_BIN)` is genuinely unread inside tools-biff (lines 161 to 185 contain no reference). It is read only by `test` on line 244.

Findings:

1. MEDIUM, Makefile:170 and 176 to 181. The new `2>&1` on the `uv tool list` capture merges streams that rows 4b and 4c classify on. Check 3's `grep -qFx` exact-line match is robust to it, but row 4b's `installed=$(printf ... | grep -F 'punt-biff ' | head -1)` on line 177 reads the merged stream. A uv stderr warning that mentions `punt-biff ` (uv emits lines such as "warning: Ignoring malformed tool `punt-biff`" and receipt warnings) written before the listing line becomes `installed`, so a situation the table files as 4c (pin listed, entrypoint missing) prints 4b's message with the warning text as the "installed version". The table claims each row is mutually exclusive; this path produces 4b's message under 4c's condition. Fix: capture stderr into the existing temp file, `listing=$$(uv tool list 2>"$$err")`, keep `listing` stdout-only for 3, 4b, 4c, and in 4a quote both `$$listing` and `cat "$$err"`. No stream is discarded and nothing in the table changes.

2. MEDIUM, Makefile:163 to 168. A path the table does not list: mktemp failing (TMPDIR unset or pointing at a missing directory). `err` is empty, the trap becomes `rm -f ""`, the redirect `2>"$$err"` fails before uv runs, `bin` is empty with `bin_status=2`, and the recipe prints "'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit 2):" followed by a `cat: ''` error. uv was never executed; the message blames it. mktemp's own stderr line does appear, so it is misattributed rather than silent. Fix: `err=$$(mktemp) || { echo "tools-biff: mktemp failed (check TMPDIR)" >&2; exit 1; }` before setting the trap, and add that row to the table.

3. MEDIUM, Makefile:234 to 241 with 244. The comment above `UVTOOL_BIN` says tools-biff "fails loudly before test ever constructs this PATH if the directory can't be determined, so by the time this is read a non-empty value means a real directory". That guarantee no longer holds: tools-biff now resolves the directory at recipe time and proceeds, while `test` still uses the parse-time value. If the parse-time `$(shell uv tool dir --bin 2>/dev/null)` returned empty (the transient case the old "re-run make" branch existed for), tools-biff reports "already installed, skipping" or installs successfully, then `test` builds a PATH without the uv bin dir and the MCP registry test fails with "biff not found" and no pointer to the cause. The round-4 retry wording was removed but the one consequence it diagnosed was not re-covered. Cheapest fix that keeps the table enumerable: after check 2 succeeds, add `if [ "$$bin" != "$(UVTOOL_BIN)" ]; then echo "tools-biff: uv bin dir resolved to $$bin at recipe time but $(UVTOOL_BIN) (empty = unresolved) at make parse time; re-run make" >&2; exit 1; fi` as a new row, or compute the PATH prefix in `test`'s recipe at recipe time instead of at parse time. Either way, also correct the comment on lines 234 to 237.

Table versus code, minor: row 3's stated condition omits "list exits 0", which the code requires on line 171. As written, rows 3 and 4a overlap (list nonzero but the pin line and entrypoint present); the code resolves it by precedence to 4a. Add "AND `uv tool list` exits 0" to row 3's condition so the table's mutual-exclusivity claim is literally true.

No other `2>/dev/null` or `2>&1` was introduced beyond line 170. No table row is unreachable.

# Outcome table -- every path this recipe can take. Review this table,
# not the shell: the rows are not all mutually exclusive (a case can
# satisfy more than one of 4a/4b/4c's conditions at once -- see below),
# so the TIEBREAKER is the fixed check order the recipe implements: 4a
# is tested before 4b, which is tested before 4c, and the first one that
# matches is the one that prints. The recipe body implements exactly
# these rows and no others.
#
# | #  | Check            | Condition                                      | Message (stderr)                                                    | Exit          |
# |----|------------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
# | 1  | uv on PATH       | `command -v uv` fails                          | "uv not found on PATH -- install uv (...) to provision biff"         | 1             |
# | 2  | bin dir known    | `mktemp` fails                                  | "mktemp failed (check TMPDIR)"                                       | 1             |
# | 2  | bin dir known    | `uv tool dir --bin` exits nonzero, OR exits 0   | "'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit N): <captured stderr>"             | 1             |
# |    |                  | with empty stdout                               |                                                                        |               |
# | 2  | bin dir known    | exits 0 with non-empty stdout                   | (none -- that stdout becomes the bin dir for checks 3-4 below)       | continues     |
# | 3  | skip decision    | entrypoint executable AND `uv tool list` exits  | "punt-biff vX already installed, skipping"                           | 0             |
# |    |                  | 0 AND shows exactly the pin                     |                                                                        |               |
# | 4a | reinstall reason | `uv tool list` exits nonzero                    | "'uv tool list' failed (exit N): <captured stdout and stderr> --     | install's own |
# |    |                  |                                                  | reinstalling anyway"                                                  |               |
# | 4b | reinstall reason | list exits 0 but listed version != pin          | "installed <version|<none>> differs from pin <pin>; reinstalling"    | install's own |
# | 4c | reinstall reason | list exits 0, pin IS listed, entrypoint missing | "biff entrypoint missing or not executable at <path> (pin <pin> is   | install's own |
# |    |                  | or not executable                               | listed); reinstalling"                                               |               |
# | 5  | install          | reached after any of 4a/4b/4c                   | `uv tool install`'s own output                                        | install's own |
#
# No `2>/dev/null` anywhere below: every uv call's stderr is either shown
# (check 2's failure) or captured into the shared temp file so the
# reinstall-reason messages can quote it (check 4's `uv tool list`),
# never discarded. `uv tool list`'s STDOUT is captured separately from
# its stderr (not merged with 2>&1): a uv warning that happens to
# mention "punt-biff " on stderr must never be readable as the installed
# version by rows 3/4b/4c, which classify on the stdout listing alone;
# row 4a is the only one that also quotes the captured stderr. Check 2
# runs `uv tool dir --bin` fresh at recipe time rather than trusting a
# parse-time variable; the `test` target below does the same
# independently, for the same reason -- a parse-time snapshot has no way
# to recover from a transient failure, so nothing in this Makefile reads
# one for the uv bin dir any more.
tools-biff: ## Install the pinned biff CLI if missing, unreachable, or out of pin (needed by internal/daemon's MCP registry test)
	@command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "tools-biff: uv not found on PATH -- install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to provision biff" >&2; exit 1; }; \
	err=$$(mktemp) || { echo "tools-biff: mktemp failed (check TMPDIR)" >&2; exit 1; }; \
	trap 'rm -f "$$err"' EXIT; \
	bin=$$(uv tool dir --bin 2>"$$err"); bin_status=$$?; \
	if [ $$bin_status -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$$bin" ]; then \
		echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit $$bin_status):" >&2; \
		cat "$$err" >&2; \
		exit 1; \
	fi; \
	listing=$$(uv tool list 2>"$$err"); list_status=$$?; \
	if [ $$list_status -eq 0 ] && test -x "$$bin/biff" && printf '%s\n' "$$listing" | grep -qFx "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)"; then \
		echo "tools-biff: punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION) already installed, skipping" >&2; \
	else \
		if [ $$list_status -ne 0 ]; then \
			echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool list' failed (exit $$list_status): stdout=$$listing stderr=$$(cat "$$err") -- reinstalling anyway" >&2; \
		else \
			installed=$$(printf '%s\n' "$$listing" | grep -F 'punt-biff ' | head -1); \
			if [ "$$installed" != "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)" ]; then \
				echo "tools-biff: installed $${installed:-<none>} differs from pin punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION); reinstalling" >&2; \
			else \
				echo "tools-biff: biff entrypoint missing or not executable at $$bin/biff (pin punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION) is listed); reinstalling" >&2; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		uv tool install --force punt-biff==$(BIFF_VERSION); \
	fi

4c -- as the tiebreaker the if/elif chain enforces; row 3's condition

required; mktemp failure is its own row.

beadle-f34m
EOF

tool_input.message:
Round-6 re-review of 8c5e704 (Makefile only): two MEDIUM findings, no CRITICAL/HIGH. All four round-5 closures verified as real. File: <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve/Makefile.

FINDING 1 — MEDIUM — Makefile:175-181 vs. the preamble claim at Makefile:158-162.
Check 2's SUCCESS-path stderr is discarded. Line 175 writes `uv tool dir --bin`'s stderr into "$err". On the row-2 "exits 0 with non-empty stdout" path nothing reads that file; line 181 then truncates it with `2>"$err"` for the list capture. So a uv warning emitted on a successful `uv tool dir --bin` (e.g. a deprecation or UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR notice) is captured and then overwritten unseen. The preamble says every uv call's stderr is "either shown (check 2's failure) or captured ... never discarded" — false for check 2's success path; the table row says "(none)" for the message, which is accurate for the recipe's own message but hides that uv's stderr vanishes. Note the overwrite is CORRECT for row 4a (it must quote only the list's stderr, and it does), so the fix is not "stop truncating" but "show row 2's stderr before truncating". Recommend after line 180 (the `fi` closing the row-2 check): `[ -s "$$err" ] && cat "$$err" >&2;` and amend the row-2 success row's message column to "(uv's own stderr, if any, passed through)". Also amend the preamble sentence accordingly.

FINDING 2 — MEDIUM — Makefile:255-259 (the `test` recipe's own resolution).
The recipe-time `uv tool dir --bin` discards its exit status: `uvbin=$$(uv tool dir --bin)` is followed only by `[ -z "$$uvbin" ]`. Two consequences: (a) a nonzero exit with non-empty stdout proceeds and puts that stdout on PATH; (b) a nonzero exit with empty stdout is reported as "'uv tool dir --bin' produced no output at recipe time", which misattributes a failure as an empty result and omits the exit status that row 2 of tools-biff reports for the identical probe. Its stderr is NOT silent — it is unredirected, so uv's message lands on the terminal just above the make error — and the failure IS distinguishable from biff genuinely missing (it exits before go test with a message naming uv tool dir). So this is a classification/consistency defect, not a swallowed error. Recommend mirroring row 2 exactly: `uvbin=$$(uv tool dir --bin); st=$$?; if [ $$st -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$$uvbin" ]; then echo "test: 'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit $$st) or produced no output -- cannot build the PATH that carries biff" >&2; exit 1; fi;`.

VERIFIED CLEAN (specific questions from your brief):
- mktemp guard under set-e-less recipes: `err=$$(mktemp) || { ...; exit 1; }` — the status of an assignment whose value is a command substitution IS the substitution's status (POSIX 2.9.1). Tested empirically with a failing mktemp under dash (this host's /bin/sh) and bash: the guard fires and the shell exits 1 in both. Trap is set only after the guard (line 174), so a failed mktemp never installs `rm -f ""`.
- Same shell for PATH: lines 255-260 are one recipe joined by `; \`, so `uvbin` is in scope for the go test line. Confirmed.
- Temp-file reuse overwriting row-2 stderr: the only consumer of row-2's stderr is the failure branch at 177-180, which cats it and exits before line 181. Nothing that still needs it is overwritten. (The success-path loss is Finding 1.)
- Row 4a: quotes both `$$listing` (stdout) and `$$(cat "$$err")` (stderr, which at that point holds only the list call's stderr). Matches the table.
- Rows 3/4a/4b/4c: code order is exactly 4a (list_status ne 0) → 4b (installed != pin, with <none> when absent) → 4c (else). Every state maps to one row; the tiebreaker text matches the if/elif chain. Row 3 requires list exit 0 AND -x AND exact pin line, matching the amended condition text. "exit 0" for row 3 holds — the skip branch falls through to `fi`.
- No remaining merged stream that classification depends on: rows 3/4b/4c read `$$listing` (stdout only). `command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1` at line 172 is not a uv call and emits nothing of value.
- No code path produces an outcome outside the table, other than the two above (row-2 success stderr, and the test recipe's unlisted "nonzero exit, non-empty stdout" path).

No files edited; tools-biff was not run.

Verdict: PASS, zero findings. Mission m-2026-10-22-040 (bead beadle-f34m), commit 8c5e704 on fix/ethos-mcp-serve, built on 8f3873b. Write set respected (Makefile only, worktree clean, one commit, nothing pushed).

Row-by-row, independently reproduced:

1. UVTOOL_BIN fully removed — `grep -n UVTOOL_BIN Makefile` is zero hits.
2. tools-biff recipe body has no `2>/dev/null`/`2>&1` on the uv calls — the only `2>&1` left is the pre-existing `command -v uv` check, unrelated to `uv tool list`.
3. Fidelity (a) — a uv shim that prints `warning: Ignoring malformed tool \`punt-biff\`` on stderr before a clean listing, with the entrypoint removed, prints row 4c ("biff entrypoint missing... pin is listed; reinstalling"), never row 4b. Confirmed the stdout-only capture (`listing=$$(uv tool list 2>"$$err")`) is what makes this true.
4. Fidelity (b) — TMPDIR pointed at a nonexistent directory with a uv-invocation-logging shim: tools-biff prints "mktemp failed (check TMPDIR)", exits before uv is ever called; the invocation log file never came into existence.
5. Fidelity (c) — grepped zero UVTOOL_BIN hits, then used a uv shim whose first `uv tool dir --bin` call fails and all subsequent calls delegate to the real binary. Under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=<shim-dir>:/usr/local/go/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`, `make test` passes all 17 packages including internal/daemon. Ran `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal -v` directly afterward: all three subtests (ethos, beadle-email, biff) PASS. This proves the `test` target's recipe-time `uvbin=$$(uv tool dir --bin)` resolution is independent of any earlier failed call — the parse-time variable is genuinely dead.
6. Edge probe, both 4b and 4c true (version mismatch + entrypoint missing): prints 4b, matching the stated tiebreaker (4a before 4b before 4c).
7. Edge probe, list fails while entrypoint exists: prints 4a, with both stdout and stderr quoted in the message — matches the table's "<captured stdout and stderr>" text for row 4a specifically.
8. Temp file cleanup: counted /tmp/tmp.* before/after a row-2 (`uv tool dir --bin`) failure — unchanged, trap fired. The mktemp-failure path has nothing to clean up by construction, since the trap is set only after mktemp succeeds (confirmed by reading the recipe: the `|| { ...; exit 1; }` guard precedes `trap ... EXIT`).
9. `make -n test` vs 8f3873b (swapped the Makefile in the worktree temporarily, captured, restored, diffed): identical except exactly the claimed lines — the mktemp guard, the separated stderr capture, the stdout+stderr quoting in row 4a's message, and the test target's PATH-construction block (recipe-time `uvbin=$$(uv tool dir --bin)` replacing the parse-time `$(UVTOOL_BIN)` substitution). No other divergence.

No findings to report. Worker's own evidence log in results.yaml matches what I independently reproduced — nothing taken on the worker's report alone. Reflection YAML written (not submitted) to <repo>/.tmp/missions/reflections/provision-r6-eval.yaml for your record. All scratch under .tmp/eval-r6 removed; host uv/tool dirs were never touched (every probe used isolated shim dirs or UV_TOOL_DIR-style isolation per the hard rule).

Recommend closing m-2026-10-22-040 as accepted.

# Controllable uv shim for mission m-2026-10-22-041 evaluation, counter
# variant: the Nth call to `uv tool dir --bin` (1-indexed, counted via
# COUNTER_FILE) gets its own exit/stdout/stderr controls so tools-biff's

# independently.
LOG="${SHIM_LOG:-/dev/null}"
echo "uv $*" >> "$LOG"

if [ "$1 $2 $3" = "tool dir --bin" ]; then
	n=0
	if [ -f "$COUNTER_FILE" ]; then
		n=$(cat "$COUNTER_FILE")
	fi
	n=$((n + 1))
	echo "$n" > "$COUNTER_FILE"
	echo "uv-dir-call #$n" >> "$LOG"
	if [ "$n" = "1" ]; then
		if [ -n "$SHIM_BIN1_STDERR" ]; then
			printf '%s\n' "$SHIM_BIN1_STDERR" >&2
		fi
		if [ -n "$SHIM_BIN1_STDOUT" ]; then

			printf '%s\n' "$SHIM_BIN2_STDOUT"
		fi
		exit "${SHIM_BIN2_EXIT:-0}"
	fi
fi

if [ "$1 $2" = "tool list" ]; then
	echo "uv-list-call" >> "$LOG"
	if [ -n "$SHIM_LIST_STDERR" ]; then
		printf '%s\n' "$SHIM_LIST_STDERR" >&2

	exit "${SHIM_INSTALL_EXIT:-0}"
fi

echo "uv shim: unhandled args: $*" >&2
exit 99

tool_input.message:
Round-7 re-review of 06fb7a8 (Makefile): both round-6 fixes verified; ONE new finding, and it is the same class as round 6's finding (1), on the other uv call.

FINDING (MEDIUM, silent discard) -- Makefile:186 + 178 + 187-199, preamble 159-164.
`uv tool list` stderr on the exit-0 paths is captured into $err and then deleted by the EXIT trap without ever being read. Rows 3, 4b, and 4c all run with list_status=0 and none of them reads $err; only row 4a (line 191) quotes it. So a uv warning emitted alongside a successful listing (exit 0, e.g. a deprecation or bin-dir-not-on-PATH warning) is captured-then-rm'd: the exact defect round 6 fixed for `uv tool dir --bin` at line 185, now on the second uv call. The preamble's "every uv call's stderr is either shown or captured ... never discarded" is false for rows 3/4b/4c: captured into a file nobody reads and the trap unlinks is discarded. The table's message column for rows 3, 4b, 4c says nothing about passthrough, so the table is also incomplete for this outcome.
Recommend, after line 186 and before line 187:
    if [ $$list_status -eq 0 ] && [ -s "$$err" ]; then cat "$$err" >&2; fi; \
(guarded on list_status so 4a does not print the stderr twice -- it already quotes it inline at 191), plus "uv's own stderr, if any, passed through" on rows 3/4b/4c and a preamble sentence saying check 4's exit-0 paths pass it through and only 4a quotes it.
Per your "recurrence on a recipe means restructure" memory: this is the second same-class finding (captured stderr unseen) on this recipe across rounds 6 and 7. Flagging the trigger; the fix itself is one line.

EVERYTHING ELSE ASKED -- confirmed, no finding:
- Line 185 `[ -s "$$err" ] && cat "$$err" >&2;` -- its status is never read. Next statement is `listing=$$(...)` and `list_status=$$?` reads the assignment's status (= the substitution's), not 185's. It cannot be the recipe's exit status on any path: it is not followed by an `exit`, and the if/else at 187-201 is the unconditional last statement, so the sh -c exit status is `echo` (0, row 3) or `uv tool install` (row 5). The EXIT trap's `rm -f` does not alter the exit status (POSIX: trap action does not replace the pending status unless it calls exit itself). Even under a future `sh -e`, a failing `[ -s ]` as the non-final member of an AND-list does not trigger errexit.
- `cat "$$err"` at 185 races nothing: the substitution at 179 waits for `uv tool dir --bin` to exit, and the `2>` fd closes with it; no other writer of $err exists between 179 and 186. (Only an orphaned uv grandchild holding the inherited fd could still write; `uv tool dir` spawns none.)
- Truncation at 186: the shell opens $err with O_TRUNC before exec'ing `uv tool list`, after 185 has already shown the prior contents, so row 4a's `$$(cat "$$err")` at 191 is exactly the list call's stderr and nothing else. Nothing lost, nothing mixed.
- `test` recipe 264-269: resolver stderr is unredirected, reaches the terminal. Message at 266 is accurate for both causes: nonzero exit prints "failed (exit N) or produced no output" with the real N and uv's stderr already on the terminal above it; exit 0 with empty stdout prints "(exit 0) or produced no output", which identifies the cause by elimination. Mirrors row 2 exactly.

UV INVOCATION ENUMERATION (both recipes):
1. L176 `command -v uv` (not uv itself): stdout/stderr -> /dev/null; consumed by row 1.
2. L179 `uv tool dir --bin 2>"$$err"`: stdout -> $bin; stderr -> $err. Failure path (row 2, L180-183): $err shown at 182, $bin discarded. Success path (row 2 continues): $bin feeds rows 3/4c/5 via "$$bin/biff"; $err passed through at L185.
3. L186 `uv tool list 2>"$$err"`: stdout -> $listing; stderr -> $err. $listing consumed by row 3 (grep -qFx), 4a (quoted), 4b (grep -F | head -1), 4c (pin-listed implied by reaching else with installed==pin). $err consumed by row 4a ONLY (L191); on rows 3/4b/4c it is unread -> the finding above.
4. L200 `uv tool install --force`: stdout and stderr unredirected -> terminal; exit status becomes the recipe's (row 5, "install's own"). Correct.
5. L264 `uv tool dir --bin` (test recipe): stdout -> $uvbin; stderr -> terminal unredirected; consumed by L265 check and the PATH at L269. No table for `test`; the one message is L266.

NOTE, not a finding (matches the table as written): row 2's failure message quotes `<captured stderr>` only, so for "exit nonzero with a stray path on stdout and empty stderr" the user sees "failed (exit N):" followed by nothing, while row 4a quotes both streams. Table and code agree; whether row 2 should also quote stdout is your call.

Every row 1-5 is reachable; no outcome outside the table other than the rows 3/4b/4c passthrough gap above. No files edited; tools-biff not run.

# Outcome table -- every path this recipe can take. Review this table,
# not the shell: the rows are not all mutually exclusive (a case can
# satisfy more than one of 4a/4b/4c's conditions at once -- see below),
# so the TIEBREAKER is the fixed check order the recipe implements: 4a
# is tested before 4b, which is tested before 4c, and the first one that
# matches is the one that prints. The recipe body implements exactly
# these rows and no others.
#
# | #  | Check            | Condition                                      | Message                                                              | Exit          |
# |----|------------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
# | 1  | uv on PATH       | `command -v uv` fails                          | "uv not found on PATH -- install uv (...) to provision biff"         | 1             |
# | 2  | bin dir known    | `uv tool dir --bin` exits nonzero, OR exits 0   | "'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit N) or produced no output (stdout:  | 1             |
# |    |                  | with empty stdout                               | <captured stdout>) -- see uv's message above"                        |               |
# | 2  | bin dir known    | exits 0 with non-empty stdout                   | (none -- that stdout becomes the bin dir for checks 3-4 below)       | continues     |
# | 3  | skip decision    | entrypoint executable AND `uv tool list` exits  | "punt-biff vX already installed, skipping"                           | 0             |
# |    |                  | 0 AND shows exactly the pin                     |                                                                        |               |
# | 4a | reinstall reason | `uv tool list` exits nonzero                    | "'uv tool list' failed (exit N) (stdout: <captured stdout>) -- see   | install's own |
# |    |                  |                                                  | uv's message above; reinstalling anyway"                              |               |
# | 4b | reinstall reason | list exits 0 but listed version != pin          | "installed <version|<none>> differs from pin <pin>; reinstalling"    | install's own |
# | 4c | reinstall reason | list exits 0, pin IS listed, entrypoint missing | "biff entrypoint missing or not executable at <path> (pin <pin> is   | install's own |
# |    |                  | or not executable                               | listed); reinstalling"                                               |               |
# | 5  | install          | reached after any of 4a/4b/4c                   | `uv tool install`'s own output                                        | install's own |
#
# The invariant that replaces per-row stderr bookkeeping: stderr is
# never redirected in this recipe (the one exception, `command -v uv
# >/dev/null 2>&1`, discards nothing of uv's -- uv is never invoked on
# that line). uv's own diagnostics reach the terminal directly, in the
# order uv wrote them, always before this recipe's own message about
# that same call -- so no row can discard them, and no row needs to
# capture, quote, or pass them through either. Only STDOUT is captured
# (`$$(...)`), so a uv warning can never be read as a listing: rows
# 3/4b/4c classify on the captured stdout alone, and the `grep -F
# 'punt-biff '` that extracts the installed line never sees anything
# uv wrote to stderr. Rows 2 and 4a quote the captured stdout in their
# own failure messages where it helps diagnose what uv returned, but
# that stdout was never stderr to begin with. An earlier version of
# this recipe captured stderr into a shared temp file so error messages
# could quote it; that created a new question on every row (has this
# row read the file yet?) and the file went unread on three separate
# occasions across three rounds. Not redirecting stderr in the first
# place removes the question instead of answering it a fourth time.
# Check 2 runs `uv tool dir --bin` fresh at recipe time rather than
# trusting a parse-time variable; the `test` target below does the same
# independently, for the same reason -- a parse-time snapshot has no way
# to recover from a transient failure, so nothing in this Makefile reads
# one for the uv bin dir any more.
tools-biff: ## Install the pinned biff CLI if missing, unreachable, or out of pin (needed by internal/daemon's MCP registry test)
	@command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "tools-biff: uv not found on PATH -- install uv (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) to provision biff" >&2; exit 1; }; \
	bin=$$(uv tool dir --bin); bin_status=$$?; \
	if [ $$bin_status -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$$bin" ]; then \
		echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit $$bin_status) or produced no output (stdout: $$bin) -- see uv's message above" >&2; \
		exit 1; \
	fi; \
	listing=$$(uv tool list); list_status=$$?; \
	if [ $$list_status -eq 0 ] && test -x "$$bin/biff" && printf '%s\n' "$$listing" | grep -qFx "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)"; then \
		echo "tools-biff: punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION) already installed, skipping" >&2; \
	else \
		if [ $$list_status -ne 0 ]; then \
			echo "tools-biff: 'uv tool list' failed (exit $$list_status) (stdout: $$listing) -- see uv's message above; reinstalling anyway" >&2; \
		else \
			installed=$$(printf '%s\n' "$$listing" | grep -F 'punt-biff ' | head -1); \
			if [ "$$installed" != "punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION)" ]; then \
				echo "tools-biff: installed $${installed:-<none>} differs from pin punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION); reinstalling" >&2; \
			else \
				echo "tools-biff: biff entrypoint missing or not executable at $$bin/biff (pin punt-biff v$(BIFF_VERSION) is listed); reinstalling" >&2; \
			fi; \
		fi; \
		uv tool install --force punt-biff==$(BIFF_VERSION); \
	fi

tool_input.message:
Round 8 (23d283d, Makefile only) has zero findings. The invariant holds by construction, and every question in your brief checks out. Details below with file:line against the commit's Makefile.

UV INVOCATIONS, ENUMERATED (every one in both recipes; nothing else in the file spawns uv):
- Makefile:181 `command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1` — shell builtin, no uv process. The redirects discard the builtin's output only.
- Makefile:182 `bin=$$(uv tool dir --bin)` — stdout captured into $bin; stderr inherited from the recipe shell (make's fd 2, the terminal). Not redirected.
- Makefile:187 `listing=$$(uv tool list)` — stdout captured into $listing; stderr inherited. Not redirected.
- Makefile:201 `uv tool install --force punt-biff==$(BIFF_VERSION)` — neither stream captured or redirected.
- Makefile:265 (test recipe) `uvbin=$$(uv tool dir --bin)` — stdout captured; stderr inherited. Not redirected.
A grep for `2>`, `>&`, `mktemp`, `trap` across lines 180-202 returns only line 181. No stream of any uv process is redirected, merged, or discarded anywhere in tools-biff. `make -n test` confirms the same after expansion: the only `2>&1` in the tools-biff block is the `command -v` line.

STDOUT-ONLY CAPTURE STILL PREVENTS STDERR MISCLASSIFICATION: yes. `$(...)` captures fd 1 only; uv's fd 2 is the recipe shell's fd 2. The classifiers at :188 (`printf '%s\n' "$$listing" | grep -qFx`) and :194 (`grep -F 'punt-biff ' | head -1`) read $listing exclusively. A stderr line containing "punt-biff " can never enter $listing. The protection came from separate capture of the two streams in 06fb7a8 and still does; the temp file was never part of it.

ORDERING OF UV'S STDERR VERSUS THE RECIPE'S ECHO: uv's diagnostic can never appear after the recipe's message about the same call. Command substitution waits for the child to exit before the assignment completes; every write(2) uv issued to fd 2 (and any flush at process exit) has happened before `$(...)` returns, and the following `echo ... >&2` writes to the same open file description. This holds on a terminal, through a pipe (`make 2>&1 | tee`), and under `--output-sync` (the recipe is one backslash-continued logical line, so even `-Oline` keeps it as one unit). One non-finding caveat: under `make -j` without output-sync, another prerequisite of `test` (tools-ethos's `go install`, tools-beadle-email's `go build`) can print between uv's line and the recipe's echo. Relative order is still preserved, so "see uv's message above" remains true; it is just not guaranteed to be immediately above. CI (test.yml:26-41) runs plain serial `make`.

ROW 2 QUOTING STDOUT ON NONZERO EXIT (:184): no wrongly trusted path. The stdout is labeled `(stdout: ...)` inside a message that opens with `failed (exit N)` and is followed by `exit 1`; the recipe never uses that value. 06fb7a8 dropped stdout on this path entirely, so this is strictly more information, not a new trust hazard. Row 4a (:192) likewise labels it and continues to reinstall, which does not depend on the quoted value.

LESS DIAGNOSABLE THAN 06fb7a8? No, on every row:
- Row 2 failure: 06fb7a8 printed a header then `cat "$err"`. Now uv's stderr prints first, directly, then the header with exit status and captured stdout. Same stderr content, plus stdout.
- Row 2 success with a warning: 06fb7a8 passed $err through after the fact. Now the warning reaches the terminal as uv writes it. Equivalent.
- Row 4a: 06fb7a8 quoted `stderr=$(cat "$err")` inline. Now uv's stderr is on the terminal immediately above, and the message says so explicitly. The one thing lost is the literal `stderr=` label binding the text to the 4a message; adjacency plus the explicit pointer is an adequate replacement given the serial run, and the parallel-make caveat above is the only way adjacency weakens.
- Rows 3/4b/4c: 06fb7a8's `uv tool list` stderr went unread on these rows (the round 6/7 class). Now it always reaches the terminal. Strictly more diagnosable.
- Row 5 and the test recipe: unchanged shape; test's message now also quotes stdout (:267).
- The mktemp failure row is gone along with the code that could fail that way; nothing lost.
Edge note, not a finding: on the "exit 0 with empty stdout" branch where uv also wrote nothing to stderr, "see uv's message above" points at nothing. 06fb7a8's `cat` of an empty file was equally empty; the message still shows `exit 0` and `stdout: ` which is the actual diagnosis.

TABLE VERSUS CODE: every row is reachable and every code path is in the table. :181 → row 1. :182-186 → row 2 fail / continue. :188-189 → row 3 (list exit 0 AND -x AND exact-line match). :191-192 → 4a. :194-196 → 4b (reached when list exits 0 and either the pin is not listed or the entrypoint is missing; the `installed != pin` test resolves it to 4b whenever the pin is absent, regardless of -x). :197-198 → 4c (pin listed, so only -x can have failed). :201 → row 5. Tiebreaker order 4a, 4b, 4c matches the nesting. Exit codes match the table: row 3 ends on `echo` (0); rows 4x end on `uv tool install` whose status is the `if` compound's status and hence the recipe's; rows 1 and 2 exit 1 explicitly. No orphan rows, no unlisted outcomes.

`make -n test` SCOPE: dry-run executes nothing (no `+` or `$(MAKE)` lines), so it touched no host uv dirs. It expands to: tools-ethos `go install`; the full tools-biff block as above; `mkdir -p` and `go build` for tools-beadle-email; then the test resolver and `PATH=... go test -race -count=1 ./...`. Confirms the single `2>&1` and the absence of mktemp/trap after expansion.

(a) mcpCommandInstallRemedy's default arm silently returned "install
    it" for an unrecognized command, so a new registry entry naming a
    binary with no provisioning story would pass the test right up
    until the first CI host without that binary on PATH, with a
    useless failure message. Changed the signature to
    (remedy string, known bool) with NO default arm, and the test
    require.True's the bool before LookPath -- a failure now names
    the exact gap (no tools-<cmd> target, no CI step, no remedy case)
    instead of silently degrading to a generic message.

(b) The usage check required only a case-insensitive "usage"
    substring, which a CLI's ROOT usage (printed on an unrecognized
    subcommand, also exiting 0) satisfies without ever reaching the
    named entry's own help text. Now requires the literal case-
    sensitive "Usage:" AND the entry's own command line (cfg.Command
    plus its Args, space-joined) in the output, tying the pass to the
    SPECIFIC subcommand this entry names.

(c) exec.CommandContext's default Cancel (SIGKILL on context done)
    only reaches the direct child; a server that forks a grandchild
    holding the inherited stdout/stderr pipe open leaves
    CombinedOutput blocked reading those pipes past the context
    deadline regardless. Set cmd.WaitDelay = time.Second so Wait stops
    waiting on descendants and returns once that delay elapses after
    the direct child exits.

Verified each against a disposable fake binary (not committed):

  subcommand text, exit 0 -- confirmed the command-line check correctly
  flags it, since "rootusage serve" never appears in that output.

tool_input.content: Invariant review of e410aa1 and 950a5f3 in the mc…
tool_input.message:
Invariant review of e410aa1 and 950a5f3 in the mcp-serve worktree: one HIGH, three MEDIUM, two notes. Both tests pass under -race on this host. Worktree is clean (git status empty), so the handler.go on-disk change notice was the can-fail proof's restore.

CONFIRMED

(1) Discriminator and timing: harness_test.go:184 branches on wantRecordStatus, not wantSpawnerCalls. "completed" is deterministic at read time: OnNewMail does h.wg.Add(1) before the go statement (handler.go:187-188), the goroutine's wg.Done is deferred after executor.Run returns (189, 210), and Run's last act before return is p.Status="completed"; e.save(p) (pipeline.go:213-214), where Save is a synchronous WriteFile+Rename (persist.go:83-86). No window with "running" on disk after Stop() unblocks.

(3) A gate-3/4 negative row {messageSigned:true, contactPerm:"rwx", wantSpawnerCalls:0, wantRecordStatus:"failed"} flows through the assertion block unchanged: require.Len(calls,0), skip tools check, require.Len(entries,1), assert Status=="failed". Verified the record would exist: unknown command -> pipeline.go:89-95 saves "failed"; contract rejected -> runner.go:62-65 errors -> pipeline.go:156-161 saves "failed". Caveat: the table has no column to induce either failure (signing at 109-142 and the planner/contract at 150-152 are hardcoded in the loop body), and line 142's require.Contains would need to become conditional for a gate-3 row. Assertion untouched; setup needs new inducement columns.

(4b) The two substrings hold for the three real outputs and no root usage satisfies both: ethos root prints "ethos [command]" and never "ethos serve"; beadle-email root never prints "beadle-email serve"; biff root prints "the biff MCP server" (capital MCP, case-sensitive Contains misses it). The subcommand lines are structural for cobra (UseLine = CommandPath) and click (ctx.command_path), not coincidence.

(5) ErrWaitDelay is a plain errors.New sentinel (exec.go:128), substituted only when err==nil, i.e. the direct child exited 0 (exec.go:870-873). errors.AsType[*exec.ExitError] is false, ctx.Err() is nil, so it lands in the generic t.Fatalf at templates_test.go:220. Correct branch. If the child exits non-zero while a grandchild holds the pipe, the *ExitError wins and the exit-code branch reports it, also correct.

FINDINGS

HIGH — templates_test.go:176-179 claims "a registry entry naming a command with no provisioning story fails outright." The known check at 197-199 only runs inside `if err != nil` after exec.LookPath (195). Falsifying case: add {Command:"quarry"} to DefaultMCPRegistry on a host where quarry is on PATH. LookPath succeeds, mcpCommandInstallRemedy is never called, the test passes locally; it fails only on a host missing the binary. Commit message (a) describes exactly this gap and the fix only improves the failure message on that host. Fix: call mcpCommandInstallRemedy(cfg.Command) and require.True(known) before LookPath, unconditionally.

MEDIUM — templates_test.go:240-241 ("There is deliberately no default arm") and commit (a) ("NO default arm") are false as written: templates_test.go:254-255 is `default: return "", false`. The enforced property is that the default arm returns known=false. Fix the prose to say that; a reader checking the claim against the switch finds a default arm.

MEDIUM — harness_test.go:180-181: "the negative rows prove a record would be written before either gate could fail them" states the ordering backwards. Gates 1 and 2 run inside OnNewMail (handler.go:149-166) before the goroutine that constructs Executor.Run exists; the record is written only after both pass. The negative rows prove no record is written when either gate rejects. The non-vacuity argument itself (fresh t.TempDir at 158, Store:nil makes save a no-op at pipeline.go:368) is sound. Fix: reword to the correct direction.

MEDIUM — templates_test.go:223 builds commandLine as cfg.Command + " " + all Args joined. Help output prints the command path, not the argv. Falsifying case: {Command:"beadle-email", Args:["serve","--transport","stdio"]} is a valid stdio entry; its --help prints "beadle-email serve [flags]", "beadle-email serve --transport stdio" never appears, and the test fails with the misleading "may be ROOT usage" diagnosis. Comment 152-154 calls this "the command line itself" and ties it to "the SPECIFIC subcommand"; it is only the subcommand path when Args carries no flags. Fix: derive the expected path from the leading non-dash Args, or make "Args is a bare subcommand path" a Validate rule so the assumption is enforced where the registry is built.

NOTES (not false claims)

- harness_test.go:164: Stop() cancels h.ctx before waiting. The only ctx-aware call on the positive path is runner.go:95's `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "ethos","mission","close",...)`; Start returns ctx.Err() immediately on a done context, so mission close never executes in this test, every run, and is logged as a Warn. "completed" holds only because close failure is non-fatal (runner.go:96-98). If close is ever made fatal, the positive row flakes on scheduling rather than failing cleanly. Worth knowing before anyone leans on this test for close coverage.

- templates_test.go:159-160 says the WaitDelay timer runs "after the context is done." Per exec.go:283, it starts at whichever comes first: context done or Wait observing child exit. The scenario commit (c) verified (return in ~1s, well before the 5s deadline) is the child-exit start, which the comment does not mention. Behaviour is correct; the description is narrower than the mechanism.

tool_input.content:
---
name: evaluator-reproduces-invariant-reviewer-falsifies
description: An evaluator that reproduces the worker's proofs can pass a test whose guarding claim is false; the invariant-completeness reviewer is the pass that falsifies claims, so it runs on every diff that asserts a guard
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-22, mission m-2026-10-22-044 (beadle-fbhp) was passed by its
evaluator with zero findings after it independently re-ran the worker's
can-fail proof and both fake-binary proofs. The invariant-completeness
reviewer on the same diff found a HIGH: the registry test's
provisioning-story check ran only inside the "binary not found" branch,
so an unprovisioned command on the local PATH passed locally and would
fail only in CI, the exact gap the commit claimed to close. I had read
the diff and missed it too.

**Why:** the evaluator and I both verified that the worker's proofs
held. They did. The proofs exercised the branch the worker wrote, not
the case the claim was about. Reproducing a proof confirms the proof;
only constructing the falsifying case tests the claim.

**How to apply:** any diff whose comment, commit message, or test name
claims to guard against a class ("fails outright", "cannot drift",
"never passes vacuously") gets the invariant-completeness reviewer, and
its brief names the claim and asks for the falsifying input. Do not
close on the evaluator's pass alone when such a claim exists. When
briefing the evaluator, ask for at least one probe the worker did not
run. Related: [[recurrence-on-a-recipe-means-restructure]],
[[list-every-file-a-criterion-touches]].

## Summary

Two beads, one rollback unit on `fix/ethos-mcp-serve`.

**beadle-f34m.** The daemon's built-in `ethos` MCP registry entry named `ethos mcp`; the installed CLI starts its stdio server with `ethos serve`. Latent until a recipe named the entry. Fixed in `templates.go`, and `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal` now runs every stdio entry's real binary with `--help` and requires exit 0, the literal `Usage:`, and the entry's own subcommand path, with the provisioning-story check run unconditionally so an entry with no `tools-<cmd>` target fails on every host. `beadle-email serve` now rejects stray positionals like `ethos serve` and `biff mcp` do.

That test needs `ethos`, `beadle-email`, and `biff` on PATH, so `make test` now provisions all three (`tools-ethos`, `tools-beadle-email` as a per-checkout self-build into `.tmp/bin`, `tools-biff` via `uv tool install`), and CI does the same before its Test step. `tools-biff` went through eight review rounds and ended as a recipe with a comment table enumerating every outcome; it captures stdout only and never redirects stderr, so uv's own diagnostics always reach the terminal. The `test` recipe resolves the uv bin dir at recipe time, not parse time.

**beadle-fbhp.** `TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd` asserted the spawner but never the store. The table now carries an expected on-disk status per row; a can-fail proof (removing `Store: h.store` from `handler.go` fails only the positive row) was re-run by the worker and independently by two evaluators.

## Demo

Run from the worktree with the real tools on PATH as `make test` provides them:

```
go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd|TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal|TestMCPCommandPath' -v ./internal/daemon/
```

All subtests PASS: three harness rows, three registry entries (ethos, beadle-email, biff) against the real binaries, four command-path cases.

Invalid input: a temporary registry entry `{Command: "sh", Args: ["-c", "true"]}` (on every host's PATH, no provisioning story) fails on `require.True(known)` before any exec:

```
command "sh" for registry entry "probe-unprovisioned-high" has no provisioning story in mcpCommandInstallRemedy -- add a tools-sh Makefile target, wire it into CI, and add a case here naming the remedy
```

Missing dependency: with `uv` off PATH, `make tools-biff` prints `tools-biff: uv not found on PATH -- install uv (...) to provision biff` and exits 1. A `--help` binary that prints only root usage without the subcommand line fails the path check; a binary that forks `sleep 30` holding stdout returns in about one second via `WaitDelay` rather than blocking to the 5s deadline.

Every `tools-biff` table row and edge probe was reproduced in isolated `UV_TOOL_DIR`/`UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR` scratch dirs by the worker and independently by the evaluator; the host install was never touched. Evidence is in the exported mission results under `.punt-labs/ethos/missions-closed/`.

`make lint-strict` from any git worktree reports six spurious gosec G204 lines with a `../../../` path prefix because the exclusion is anchored at `^internal/`; the specific lines shift between runs. The authoritative `make check` ran from the main checkout with this branch checked out and is green.
EOF

No bypass: the only skip is the `cfg.Command == ""` continue at :202-204, which runs after cfg.Validate() at :201 and before `exercised++` at :205, so every non-empty-Command entry enters t.Run and hits the known check first. `exercised` counts before t.Run, so it guards vacuity, not success. require.True uses the subtest's shadowed t, so it fails the right test.

(2) MEDIUM closed. Prose at :188-191 and the doc comment at :270-275 both say the default arm returns known=false; the switch at :284-285 does exactly that.

(3) MEDIUM closed. harness_test.go:179-182 says gates 1 and 2 run inside OnNewMail before Executor.Run and any record. handler.go: x-permission at :149-154, trust at :161-166, Executor.Run at :210 inside the goroutine; pipeline.go:67-69 writes the "running" record at the top of Run. Direction now matches.

(4) MEDIUM closed as stated, but see the two new findings below.

WaitDelay comment at templates_test.go:161-168 now names both start conditions (context done, or Wait observes the direct child exited, whichever first), matching os/exec's documented semantics. ---
name: no-per-turn-needs-list
description: Never repeat a numbered "what I need next" list or re-ask a pending ruling each turn; decide what is mine, act, and speak only for a PR link or a genuine operator decision
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-22 Jim said: "You are badgering me asking for things. Are you
the COO? Or no? What consequential question do you have for me if any.
You are building up this wall of text with your asks." Then: "You need
7 things from me, shut up" and "Do your job, fulfill your role."

I had been ending every turn with a numbered list of seven items, six
of them gated on agents, one a ruling (a signed test send for
beadle-5xog) that I kept marking "yours, no re-ask" while re-asking it
anyway. Most of the seven were not asks at all. The one that was, was
mine to decide: sending a test email from my own mailbox is an
operational call, not direction.

**Why:** the operator gates designs, demos, direction, and destruction.
A status list dressed as an ask is noise, and a repeated ask reads as
the COO refusing to decide. Jim reads the last message and acts; a wall
of gated items hides whether there is anything to act on.

**How to apply:** no per-turn needs list, ever. While agents run, say
one line or nothing. Before asking Jim anything, check it against the
four gates; if it is not one of them, decide and do it. When something
is genuinely his, ask once, in one or two lines, with my
recommendation, and never mention it again until it changes. Supersedes
the ritual that grew out of [[asks-short-and-clear]].
