Verdict: PASS. All six checks constructed independently of the worker's own probes came out as designed; no findings. Reflection drafted (not submitted) at <repo>/.tmp/missions/reflections/harness-r3-eval.yaml.

Finding A (leading-flag refusal):
- {ethos, ["-v","serve"]} (single-dash short flag) — refused before exec, templates_test.go:227, exact message naming the rule.
- {ethos, ["--help"]} (Args of exactly one leading-flag element) — also refused before exec, same guard.
- {beadle-email, ["serve","--transport","stdio"]} (legitimate trailing flag) — NOT refused; ran the full subtest to completion (provisioning check, LookPath, exec --help, usage-line match) and passed cleanly. No partial-failure or later breakage.
All three probes reverted via `git checkout --`; `git diff --stat` on templates.go empty each time.

Finding B (usageLine anchoring):
- Cobra-shaped fake binary on a scratch .tmp/ PATH printing "Usage:\n\n  fakeroot serve [flags]\n..." (Usage: line, then a BLANK line, then the path) — PASSED, as the contract requires: usageLine's "next non-blank line" skip correctly jumps the blank line and finds the path.
- Second fake printing "Usage:\n  fakeroot [command]\n  fakeroot serve\n..." (an unrelated non-blank line immediately after Usage:, path only one line further) — FAILED with the exact "may be ROOT usage from an unrecognized subcommand" message, as the contract requires: usageLine only ever captures the single immediate next non-blank line, so the path one line further never enters the match.
Both registered with a temporary remedy-case edit to templates_test.go's mcpCommandInstallRemedy; both reverted, diff --stat empty after each.

usageLine edge cases (item 3): no "Usage:" anywhere in the output returns "" — and the caller's `if line == ""` check is the sole gate for that case, genuinely reachable, nothing upstream shadows it. "Usage:" appearing twice returns the FIRST occurrence joined with its own next non-blank line; the second occurrence is ignored entirely — consistent with the doc comment's "first line containing Usage:".

Items 4-6: TestUsageLine (3/3) and TestMCPCommandPath (6/6, including both new rows) all pass. The three real subtests (ethos, beadle-email, biff) pass against real binaries on PATH. Write set is templates_test.go only, one commit (1a3e351 on 1b9d4a2), worktree clean before/after every probe. make vet, staticcheck, test (-race -count=1, all packages ok), and docs are all green. make lint-strict from the worktree shows the six G204 lines, all inside internal/secret/keychain_linux.go and internal/testenv/gpg.go — both named in .golangci.yml's exclusion path — reported with worktree-relative "../../../" prefixes; re-ran lint-strict from the main checkout and got 0 issues, confirming these are the known nested-worktree gosec artifact, not real findings.

Recommend closing the mission.

tool_input.message:
Re-review of 1a3e351 (templates_test.go): one HIGH, two MEDIUM, plus confirmations. File: <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve/internal/daemon/templates_test.go

FINDING 1 (HIGH): the leading-flag guard closes Args[0] only; a flag between path elements reopens the same hole one level down.
Claim: lines 175-184 ("stdio entries must lead with the subcommand, with any flags following it") and line 227's `strings.HasPrefix(cfg.Args[0], "-")`.
Falsifying entry: {Command: "ethos", Args: ["mission", "--json", "nosuch"]}. It satisfies the guard's own rule (leads with a subcommand, flag follows). mcpCommandPath (line 280) stops at "--json" and returns "ethos mission". Measured on this host: `ethos mission --json nosuch --help` exits 0 and prints "Usage:\n  ethos mission [command]". usageLine returns "Usage:   ethos mission [command]", which contains "ethos mission", so the subtest PASSES although "nosuch" is not a subcommand. That is exactly the "ethos mcp" class this test exists for.
Related comment inaccuracy, lines 149-152: "a CLI that falls back to its ROOT usage on an unrecognized subcommand also prints that word and exits 0". Measured: `ethos nosuchcmd --help` and `biff nosuchcmd --help` both exit 2 (cobra "unknown command", click "No such command"). The exit-0 fallback for these three tools is a cobra PARENT's usage on an unknown nested subcommand (`ethos mission nosuch --help` exits 0). The anchored check catches that case only when no flag truncates the path; with a flag it does not.
Fix (either is structural): (a) forbid flags in Args entirely in this test (no element starts with "-"); no registry entry has one today, mcpCommandPath becomes cmd + all args, and the "flags follow the subcommand" rule is dropped because flag values ("stdio") are indistinguishable by shape from path elements, so a positional guard cannot be written correctly. Or (b) keep flags and add a leaf check: the usage window must not contain a subcommand placeholder ("[command]" in cobra, "COMMAND" in click). Parent and root usage always carry one; leaf usage never does. (b) also makes the root exclusion in question (3) structural rather than content-based.
Minor under the same claim: an empty-string Args[0] passes the guard (HasPrefix("", "-") is false). It is caught downstream only by accident: on cobra, `ethos "" serve --help` exits 0 with "ethos serve" usage, and the test fails only because mcpCommandPath produces "ethos  serve" (double space) with the misleading "may be ROOT usage" message; on click it exits 2. Whichever fix you take, also refuse empty elements. Args[0] == "--" is refused by the current predicate, which is correct.

FINDING 2 (MEDIUM): for click-shaped output the window includes one line of prose, so the biff root exclusion is still content-based.
Claim: lines 291-299 and 159-162 ("anchors the check to the Usage: line itself"). usageLine (lines 306-313) joins the next non-blank line unconditionally. For cobra that line is the path; for click/typer the path is already on the Usage: line, so the joined line is the first description line. Measured biff root: window = "Usage: biff [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...  Biff: the dog that barked when messages arrived." It excludes "biff mcp" only because the root docstring does not say "biff mcp". A root docstring reading "Run biff mcp to start the server" would pass the check. The test row at lines 385-393 pins this join as the expected result.
Fix: join the next line only when nothing follows "Usage:" on the matched line (strings.TrimSpace of the remainder is empty). The window is then exactly the usage path for both shapes. Update the click-shaped row's want to "Usage: biff mcp [OPTIONS]".

FINDING 3 (MEDIUM): "Usage:" is matched by Contains on the first line containing it, so prose can capture the window.
Claim: line 142 ("ON THE USAGE LINE") and line 303's `strings.Contains(line, "Usage:")`. Cobra prints a command's Long description BEFORE the usage block (ethos mission's Long already contains quoted command invocations). A Long containing "Usage:" mid-sentence becomes the window; the real usage block is never read. Today none of the three tools does this (one "Usage:" line in every output, measured). Direction is mostly fail-safe (window holds prose, path absent, test fails with a misleading message), but a Long that mentions the path right after "Usage:" would pass on prose.
Fix: anchor with strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimSpace(line), "Usage:"). Cobra ("Usage:" at column 0) and typer (" Usage: biff mcp", one leading space) both satisfy it; a mid-sentence "Usage:" does not.

Question (2), other frameworks: urfave/cli prints "USAGE:", argparse "usage:", Go flag "Usage of x:"; none matches the case-sensitive "Usage:", so an entry built on them fails loudly with "printed no Usage: line" (line 259). Safe direction, inaccurate message. No framework among the three tools or any plausible stdio entry puts the path somewhere other than the Usage: line or the next line; cobra's runnable-parent template prints the UseLine first, so that is covered too.

Question (5): lines 166-173 now state the double-fork scenario parenthetically as a fact about a review fake and say "not a committed test". Satisfied. The WaitDelay semantics described match os/exec's documentation.

Confirmed: the guard at line 227 sits after the remedy check and before LookPath, exec, and the path check, inside the same subtest with require, so every entry reaching line 262 has passed it. The three real subtests pass with -race in the worktree.

cd <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
test(daemon): stop parsing flags around the registry entry's path

Round 4 of the invariant-completeness review on 1a3e351. Rounds 2 and
3 each closed the previous round's usage-check gap and the reviewer
found the same class a third time: the check could still be satisfied
by a PARENT's or ROOT's usage. Round 3's residue: a flag planted
BETWEEN path elements (`ethos mission --json nosuch`) truncates
mcpCommandPath's output to "ethos mission" and still exits 0 on the
parent's own usage; the click join appended a prose line
unconditionally; "Usage:" was matched by Contains anywhere in the
line, so prose mentioning the word before the real block could
satisfy it; and an empty Args element passed the leading-dash guard.

The fix changes approach rather than patching another parsing edge
case: stop parsing flags out of Args at all.

1. Args is forbidden from containing a flag or an empty element,
   checked per-element: `require.True(t, a != "" && !strings.HasPrefix(a, "-"), ...)`
   for every a in cfg.Args, with a message naming why no positional
   rule can be written correctly (a flag VALUE is indistinguishable
   by shape from a path element without parsing the tool's own flag
   grammar). mcpCommandPath is now simply cmd plus every element of
   args, space-joined -- there is no flag to stop at, because the
   check above guarantees none exists. TestMCPCommandPath drops its
   now-impossible leading-flag and trailing-flag rows and pins
   {serve}, {mission,show}, {} (bare command).

2. isLeafUsage(window string) bool excludes a parent's or root's
   usage by STRUCTURE: cobra marks a non-leaf with the "[command]"
   placeholder, click marks its root with "COMMAND". Either present
   means the window is an invitation to pick a subcommand, not help
   for a specific one -- this is what actually excludes root/parent
   usage, not the path substring check, which a parent's own
   "Available Commands" prose can satisfy by naming a real
   subcommand. Corrected the comment's false claim that falling back
   to root usage exits 0: for these three tools an unknown ROOT
   subcommand exits 2 (`ethos nosuch`, `biff nosuch`, both measured);
   the exit-0 case that matters is a cobra PARENT's own usage on an
   unknown NESTED subcommand.

3. usageLine now anchors to a line whose TrimSpace starts with the
   literal "Usage:" (not Contains, so a mid-sentence mention before
   the real block cannot match), and joins the next non-blank line
   ONLY when nothing already follows "Usage:" on that line -- cobra
   needs the join (the path is on the next line); click does not (the
   path is already on the Usage: line), and joining unconditionally
   pulled a click leaf's following prose line into the window. The
   no-usage-line failure message now states the literal requirement
   and names three frameworks that would not satisfy it: urfave/cli
   ("USAGE:"), argparse ("usage:"), Go's flag package ("Usage of").

Table rows added/kept per the contract: TestUsageLine covers a cobra
leaf, a click leaf, prose-only, "Usage:" mid-sentence before the real
block, a click line with trailing prose (must not join), and no
Usage: line at all. TestIsLeafUsage covers a cobra leaf (true), a
cobra parent naming "[command]" (false), and a click root naming
"COMMAND" (false).

Proved all three required cases, each with a temporary registry entry
in templates.go reverted immediately after (git diff --stat empty,
confirmed three times):

  {ethos, ["mission","--json","nosuch"]} -- refused on the per-element
  Args check:
    templates_test.go:252: Error: Should be true
    Messages: registry entry "probe-between-flag": Args [mission --json
    nosuch] contains "--json" -- Args is the subcommand path only, no
    flags and no empty elements (a flag value is indistinguishable by
    shape from a path element, so no positional rule can single one
    out correctly)

  {ethos, ["mission","nosuch"]} -- no flag, parent usage exits 0,
  fails on the placeholder check:
    templates_test.go:289: registry entry "probe-parent-usage": ethos
    mission nosuch --help exited 0, but its usage window "Usage: ethos
    mission [command]" names a subcommand placeholder ("[command]" or
    "COMMAND") -- this is a PARENT's or ROOT's usage on an
    unrecognized subcommand, not help for the entry's own leaf command

  {ethos, ["", "serve"]} -- refused on the empty-element rule:
    templates_test.go:252: Error: Should be true
    Messages: registry entry "probe-empty-element": Args [ serve]
    contains "" -- Args is the subcommand path only, no flags and no
    empty elements (a flag value is indistinguishable by shape from a
    path element, so no positional rule can single one out correctly)

Full proof transcripts saved to
.tmp/missions/results/050-proof-{A,B,C}-*.txt (not committed). Scratch
during this mission stayed under the checkout's .tmp/, never /tmp.

go test ./internal/daemon/... -run TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal
-v: all three real subtests (ethos, beadle-email, biff) PASS. go test
-race -count=1 ./internal/daemon/ is green.

Refs beadle-fbhp.
EOF
)"

tool_input.message:
Verdict: PASS. Mission m-2026-10-22-050 (bead beadle-fbhp), commit b652336 on the mcp-serve worktree, closes round 4 clean. Reflection written to .tmp/missions/reflections/harness-r4-eval.yaml (not submitted, per your instruction).

What I checked beyond the worker's own report:

1. Per-element Args rule (internal/daemon/templates_test.go:252). Built a probe subtest, reverted after (git diff --stat empty both times):
   - `{serve, "--"}` is correctly refused (non-empty but has the leading dash).
   - `{mission, " "}` (a single-space element) is NOT refused — it's non-empty and has no leading "-", so it passes the guard silently. This is a real edge the contract's own criterion anticipated ("a whitespace-only element... report either way"). I'm reporting it as non-blocking: DefaultMCPRegistry's Args are compile-time string literals, there's no entry today with a stray-whitespace element, and no realistic typo path produces one without also producing an empty string (which the same guard does catch). Worth a one-line follow-up (`strings.TrimSpace(a) == ""`) but not worth reopening this round for.

2. isLeafUsage with a legitimate "COMMAND" in leaf prose. Built a fake binary (`fake serve --help` → `"Usage:\n  fake serve [OPTIONS]\n\n  Runs the COMMAND loop.\n"`, blank line before the prose) under the worktree's own `.tmp/`, ran it through usageLine + isLeafUsage, reverted the probe after. Result: window = `"Usage: fake serve [OPTIONS]"`, isLeaf=true. The conditional join (join only when nothing follows "Usage:" on its own line) stops at the first blank line reached via the "skip blank, take next non-blank" loop — it never walks far enough to touch the COMMAND-bearing prose line two lines down, because it returns on the very first non-blank line it meets. Then built:
   - fake cobra parent printing `"Usage:\n  fake mission [command]\n"` → window has `[command]`, isLeaf=false. Correctly fails.
   - fake click root printing `"Usage: fake [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...\n"` → window has `COMMAND`, isLeaf=false. Correctly fails.

3. usageLine mid-sentence-before-real-block and trailing-prose rows: present verbatim in the committed table (TestUsageLine, two separate subtests) and pass — confirmed by reading and by the `-run` execution below, not just by grep.

4. mcpCommandPath is cmd plus every arg, space-joined (templates.go:307-309) — read directly, and TestMCPCommandPath pins exactly `{serve}→"ethos serve"`, `{mission,show}→"ethos mission show"`, `{}→"sh"` (bare command). All three pass.

5. Ran `go test ./internal/daemon/... -run 'TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal|TestUsageLine|TestIsLeafUsage|TestMCPCommandPath' -v`: all real subtests (ethos, beadle-email, biff) and every table row across the three unit tests pass.

6. Gates, all from the worktree: `make vet` clean, `make staticcheck` clean, `make test` (full suite, -race) all green across every package, `make docs` 0 issues, `make lint-strict` 0 issues (the six G204 exclusions are path-scoped `.golangci.yml` rules for internal/pgp, internal/secret, internal/testenv, internal/daemon, internal/daemontest, cmd/beadle-email — confirmed by reading the config, not findings against this diff). One commit (b652336), write set is templates_test.go only (`git diff --stat 1a3e351..b652336` touches only that file), worktree verified clean before every probe and after every revert.

No findings rise to a blocking severity. The one whitespace-element gap is the only thing I'd flag, and only as a follow-up, not a round-5 trigger — it doesn't let a parent/root/flag-bearing usage through, which is the defect class this whole round-chain has been closing.

tool_input.message:
Round 4 of templates_test.go (b652336) closes the parent/root usage class except for one constructible case. All three real entries pass under -race -count=1 in the worktree; the Makefile and CI provisioning claims check out; worktree clean.

CRITICAL (constructible today, low likelihood): whitespace-only trailing Args element. templates_test.go:252 accepts " " (non-empty, no dash). `ethos serve " " --help` measured: exit 0, leaf usage. mcpCommandPath at :308 does TrimSpace("ethos serve  ") = "ethos serve", which the window contains, so {ethos, ["serve"," "]} PASSES while runtime `ethos serve " "` exits 2 unknown command. Fix: per-element require a == strings.TrimSpace(a) && a != ""; build mcpCommandPath as strings.Join(append([]string{cmd}, args...), " ") with no TrimSpace; add the proof.

MEDIUM, prose misattribution (:164-169, :365-369): "isLeafUsage ... is what actually excludes root/parent usage, not the path substring check" is now false. With flags banned, cmdPath contains every element, so `ethos mission nosuch` is rejected by the path check alone (window "ethos mission [command]" cannot contain "ethos mission nosuch"); proof B proves nothing about isLeafUsage. The case isLeafUsage uniquely catches is an entry naming a NON-RUNNABLE group exactly, e.g. {ethos, ["mission"]}: exit 0, path contained, only "[command]" rejects it. Undocumented and unproven; add as proof D.

MEDIUM, runnable cobra parent (:141-144, :164-166): cobra prints TWO usage lines for a runnable parent ("fake mission [flags]" then "fake mission [command]"); usageLine joins one line, so the window omits the placeholder and isLeafUsage says leaf. Net behavior is correct (a runnable parent really runs; an unknown nested word under it fails the path check), but the comment says the placeholder excludes "a parent's" usage, which is false for this shape. Document that the first-line-only window is deliberate, or someone will join the block and wrongly reject runnable-parent servers.

MEDIUM, false negatives misdiagnosed (:288-291): a leaf whose usage contains COMMAND or [command] is rejected with "this is a PARENT's or ROOT's usage". Measured: `ethos help --help` prints "Usage: ethos help [command] [flags]"; click positional metavar COMMAND and clap "[COMMAND]" (uv run) are the same. Loud, not silent; low risk for a stdio entry. Message should say "names a placeholder" without asserting what the command is.

MEDIUM, factual (:157-158): "For these three tools an unknown ROOT subcommand exits 2". beadle-email nosuch exits 1. ethos and biff exit 2 as stated. Nothing enforced on it.

Per-element completeness: "--" and "-" rejected by the dash rule; embedded-space element ("mission show") fails loudly with exit 2 from both cobra and click; leading/trailing-space elements fail at exit code or on the [command] window. Only the whitespace-only gap above survives.

Shapes measured: cobra leaf "Usage:\n  ethos serve [flags]"; cobra parent/root "Usage:\n  ethos mission [command]" / "ethos [command]"; click leaf " Usage: biff mcp [OPTIONS]" (leading space, TrimSpace handles it); click group/root "Usage: biff hook [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]..." / "biff [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...", and both click non-leaf shapes exit 2 on an unknown nested word anyway. Click leaf and cobra leaf with a stray positional both exit 0 with leaf usage; the path check catches them because cmdPath carries the stray word.

cd <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
test(daemon): close the whitespace gap and fix four prose errors

Round 5 of the invariant-completeness review on b652336. Round 4
closed the parent/root class structurally (confirmed by both
reviewers); what remained was one constructible gap and four prose
errors in the comments describing the fix.

Whitespace gap: a whitespace-only Args element (e.g. {"serve", " "})
passed the old per-element guard (non-empty, no leading "-") and
mcpCommandPath's TrimSpace then collapsed the joined path to "ethos
serve" -- identical to the real leaf {"serve"} -- even though
`ethos serve " "` is a different, failing invocation at runtime
(measured: exits 2, "unknown command"). Fixed the rule to
`a != "" && a == strings.TrimSpace(a) && !strings.HasPrefix(a, "-")`
and removed mcpCommandPath's TrimSpace entirely, so a whitespace-only
element can neither pass the guard nor be silently repaired by the
join. TestMCPCommandPath gains a row pinning the no-trim behavior.
Proved with a temporary {ethos, ["serve", " "]} entry:

  templates_test.go:255: Error: Should be true
  Messages: registry entry "probe-whitespace": Args [serve  ] contains
  " " -- Args is the subcommand path only, no flags and no empty or
  whitespace-only elements (a flag value is indistinguishable by shape
  from a path element, so no positional rule can single one out
  correctly)

Four prose fixes:

1. The main comment's second bullet credited isLeafUsage with
   excluding BOTH a non-runnable group's usage AND an unknown nested
   subcommand under a real leaf. With flags now banned from Args,
   only the first is isLeafUsage's job -- the second
   ({ethos, ["mission", "nosuch"]}) is already rejected by the path
   check alone, since the parent's identical usage window contains
   "ethos mission" but not "ethos mission nosuch". Reworded to credit
   each check for what it actually does, and added the non-runnable-
   group case, {ethos, ["mission"]}, as a proof (the path check cannot
   reject it -- the window genuinely contains "ethos mission" -- so
   isLeafUsage is what has to):

     templates_test.go:292: registry entry "probe-nonrunnable-group":
     ethos mission --help exited 0, but its usage window "Usage: ethos
     mission [command]" names a subcommand placeholder...

2. Documented, in usageLine's doc comment, why the usage window is
   deliberately one line even though cobra prints two for a command
   that is both runnable and a parent of subcommands ("Usage:\n  x
   [flags]\n  x [command]"). Reading only the first line means the
   placeholder from the second never reaches isLeafUsage, so a
   runnable parent is correctly treated as a leaf -- widening the join
   to read both lines would reject every runnable-parent server's
   registry entry on the placeholder alone, which this test must not
   do. Verified against the real ethos binary: `ethos identity --help`
   is exactly this shape ("Usage:\n  ethos identity [flags]\n  ethos
   identity [command]").

3. The placeholder-check failure message no longer asserts the command
   IS a parent or root; a leaf can legitimately print "[command]" or
   "COMMAND" too (cobra's own help command, a click metavar, clap's
   USAGE line), so the message now says a placeholder was found and
   that this usually means a group, loudly flagging the ambiguity
   rather than asserting a diagnosis the test cannot actually prove.

4. Corrected "an unknown ROOT subcommand exits 2" (previously stated
   for ethos and biff only, implying all three tools agree) --
   measured directly: `beadle-email nosuch` exits 1, not 2. isLeafUsage's
   doc comment now states each tool's measured exit code and is
   explicit that nothing in this test enforces any of them; the figures
   are cited only to explain why isLeafUsage never needs to resolve a
   root-subcommand ambiguity for these three tools.

Both proofs used a temporary entry in templates.go, reverted
immediately with git checkout (git diff --stat empty, confirmed twice
separately). Full proof transcripts saved under
.tmp/missions/results/053-proof-{whitespace,nonrunnable-group}.txt
(not committed). All scratch for this mission stayed under the
checkout's .tmp/.

go test ./internal/daemon/... -run TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal
-v: all three real subtests (ethos, beadle-email, biff) PASS. go test
-race -count=1 ./internal/daemon/ is green.

Refs beadle-fbhp.
EOF
)"

  entry {"serve"} -- even though `ethos serve " "` is a DIFFERENT,
  failing invocation at runtime. Measured directly on this host:
  `ethos serve " "` exits 2 ("unknown command \" \" for \"ethos
  serve\""). Fixed the rule to
  `a != "" && a == strings.TrimSpace(a) && !strings.HasPrefix(a, "-")`
  and removed mcpCommandPath's TrimSpace entirely (now a plain
  strings.Join with no normalization), so a whitespace-only element
  can neither pass the guard nor be silently repaired by the join.
  TestMCPCommandPath gained a row pinning the no-trim behavior:
  {"serve", " "} -> "ethos serve  " (the literal, untrimmed join).

  Proved per the contract: temporarily added {Command: "ethos", Args:
  ["serve", " "]} to DefaultMCPRegistry in templates.go. The new
  per-element rule failed on it:

    templates_test.go:255: Error: Should be true
    Messages: registry entry "probe-whitespace": Args [serve  ]
    contains " " -- Args is the subcommand path only, no flags and no
    empty or whitespace-only elements (a flag value is
    indistinguishable by shape from a path element, so no positional
    rule can single one out correctly)

  Reverted templates.go with git checkout; git diff --stat produced no
  output (confirmed empty).

  Four prose fixes, all in templates_test.go's comments:

  1. The main comment's bullet on isLeafUsage overstated its role,
  crediting it with excluding BOTH a non-runnable group's usage
  ({ethos, ["mission"]}) AND an unknown nested subcommand under a real
  leaf ({ethos, ["mission", "nosuch"]}). With flags now banned from
  Args (round 4), the second case is already rejected by the path
  check alone: `ethos mission nosuch --help` prints the SAME parent
  usage window as `ethos mission --help` ("Usage: ethos mission
  [command]"), which does not contain the configured path "ethos
  mission nosuch" -- isLeafUsage plays no role there. Reworded to
  credit each check for what it actually does, and added the
  non-runnable-group case as the proof isLeafUsage actually needs
  (below), since the path check genuinely cannot reject that one on
  its own (the window DOES contain "ethos mission").

  Proved per the contract: temporarily added {Command: "ethos", Args:
  ["mission"]} to templates.go. The command exits 0 (ethos mission
  with no subcommand prints its own group usage and a command list)
  and the path check passes (the window literally contains "ethos
  mission"), but isLeafUsage correctly rejects it on the "[command]"
  placeholder:

    templates_test.go:292: registry entry "probe-nonrunnable-group":
    ethos mission --help exited 0, but its usage window "Usage: ethos
    mission [command]" names a subcommand placeholder ("[command]" or
    "COMMAND") -- this is usually a non-runnable group's usage,
    inviting a subcommand choice rather than naming one specific
    command, but a LEAF command can legitimately print one of these
    words too...

  Reverted templates.go with git checkout; git diff --stat produced no
  output (confirmed empty, checked separately from proof 1).

  2. Documented in usageLine's doc comment why its window is
  deliberately ONE line (or "Usage:" plus one joined line) and never
  more, even though cobra prints TWO usage lines for a command that is
  both runnable and a parent of subcommands
  ("Usage:\n  x [flags]\n  x [command]"). Verified this shape exists
  in the real ethos binary: `ethos identity --help` prints exactly
  "Usage:\n  ethos identity [flags]\n  ethos identity [command]".
  usageLine reading only the first line means the placeholder from the
  second never reaches isLeafUsage, so a runnable parent is correctly
  treated as a leaf; widening the join to read both lines would reject
  every runnable-parent server's registry entry on the placeholder
  alone, which this test must not do (a runnable parent is a real
  server the entry is entitled to invoke).

  3. The placeholder-check failure message previously asserted the
  command WAS a parent's or root's usage. Corrected: it no longer
  asserts a diagnosis the test cannot actually prove, since a LEAF
  command can legitimately print "[command]" or "COMMAND" too (cobra's
  own help command, a click metavar, clap's USAGE line) -- the message
  now says a placeholder was found, that this usually means a group,
  and flags the ambiguity loudly rather than silently assuming the
  group case.

  4. Corrected the false "unknown ROOT subcommand exits 2" claim,
  which implied agreement across all three tools. Measured directly:
  `beadle-email nosuch` exits 1, not 2 ("Error: unknown command
  \"nosuch\" for \"beadle-email\"", exit 1); ethos and biff both still
  exit 2. isLeafUsage's doc comment now states each tool's measured
  exit code individually and is explicit that nothing in this test
  enforces any of them -- the figures are cited only to explain why
  isLeafUsage never needs to resolve a root-subcommand ambiguity for
  these three tools (none of them exits 0 on an unknown root
  subcommand, so there is no leaf-vs-non-leaf question to answer
  there).

  .tmp/missions/results/053-proof-{whitespace,nonrunnable-group}.txt
  (not part of the commit). All scratch for this mission stayed under

tool_input.body:
## Summary

Two beads, one rollback unit on `fix/ethos-mcp-serve`.

**beadle-f34m.** The daemon's built-in `ethos` MCP registry entry named `ethos mcp`; the installed CLI starts its stdio server with `ethos serve`. Latent until a recipe named the entry. Fixed in `templates.go`, and `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal` now runs every stdio entry's real binary with `--help` and requires exit 0, the literal `Usage:`, and the entry's own subcommand path, with the provisioning-story check run unconditionally so an entry with no `tools-<cmd>` target fails on every host. `beadle-email serve` now rejects stray positionals like `ethos serve` and `biff mcp` do.

That test needs `ethos`, `beadle-email`, and `biff` on PATH, so `make test` now provisions all three (`tools-ethos`, `tools-beadle-email` as a per-checkout self-build into `.tmp/bin`, `tools-biff` via `uv tool install`), and CI does the same before its Test step. `tools-biff` went through eight review rounds and ended as a recipe with a comment table enumerating every outcome; it captures stdout only and never redirects stderr, so uv's own diagnostics always reach the terminal. The `test` recipe resolves the uv bin dir at recipe time, not parse time.

**beadle-fbhp.** `TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd` asserted the spawner but never the store. The table now carries an expected on-disk status per row; a can-fail proof (removing `Store: h.store` from `handler.go` fails only the positive row) was re-run by the worker and independently by two evaluators.

## Demo

Run from the worktree with the real tools on PATH as `make test` provides them:

```
go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd|TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal|TestMCPCommandPath' -v ./internal/daemon/
```

All subtests PASS: three harness rows, three registry entries (ethos, beadle-email, biff) against the real binaries, four command-path cases.

Invalid input: a temporary registry entry `{Command: "sh", Args: ["-c", "true"]}` (on every host's PATH, no provisioning story) fails on `require.True(known)` before any exec:

```
command "sh" for registry entry "probe-unprovisioned-high" has no provisioning story in mcpCommandInstallRemedy -- add a tools-sh Makefile target, wire it into CI, and add a case here naming the remedy
```

Missing dependency: with `uv` off PATH, `make tools-biff` prints `tools-biff: uv not found on PATH -- install uv (...) to provision biff` and exits 1. With a `uv tool dir --bin` shim that exits 0 with empty stdout, row 2 fails with `'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit 0) or produced no output (stdout: ) -- see uv's message above`.

Boundary: `beadle-email serve bogus` now exits non-zero before any IMAP dial (`TestServeCmd_RejectsStrayPositional` drives `rootCmd.Execute()`). A `--help` binary that prints only root usage without the subcommand line fails the path check; a binary that forks `sleep 30` holding stdout returns in about one second via `WaitDelay` rather than blocking to the 5s deadline.

Finding 2 (templates_test.go:264 / Makefile / release.yml): TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal now needs ethos, beadle-email, and biff on PATH, but only the `test` target provisions them. `test-integration` (Makefile:272) and `cover` (Makefile:319) run `./...` bare, and `.github/workflows/release.yml:20-21` runs `go test -race -count=1 ./...` after only checkout and setup-go, so the next tag's release job fails on a clean runner. # The classification below mirrors tools-biff's row 2 exactly -- exit
# status AND non-empty stdout, not either alone -- so a nonzero exit
# with a stray path on stdout is treated the same way here as there:
# a failure, not a usable bin dir.
#
# TEST_PREREQS and TEST_RUN are the one shared copy of "provision ethos,
# biff, and this branch's own beadle-email, then run go test with all
# three on PATH" -- every target that runs ./... (test, test-integration,
# cover) depends on TEST_PREREQS and calls TEST_RUN so there is exactly
# one PATH= line and one provisioning prerequisite list in this file.
# Before this consolidation, test-integration and cover ran `go test
# ./...` with neither the tools-* prerequisites nor the PATH prefix,
# so any package needing ethos/biff/beadle-email on PATH (e.g.
# internal/daemon's MCP registry test) passed under `make test` and
# failed under `make test-integration`/`make cover` on an otherwise
# identical tree -- the same gap release.yml had, calling bare `go test`
# with no provisioning step at all.
TEST_PREREQS := tools-ethos tools-biff tools-beadle-email

define TEST_RUN
	uvbin=$$(uv tool dir --bin); uvbin_status=$$?; \
	if [ $$uvbin_status -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$$uvbin" ]; then \
		echo "$@: 'uv tool dir --bin' failed (exit $$uvbin_status) or produced no output (stdout: $$uvbin) -- cannot build the PATH that carries biff" >&2; \
		exit 1; \
	fi; \
	PATH="$(BEADLE_EMAIL_BIN):$(GOINSTALL_BIN):$$uvbin:$$PATH" $(1)
endef

test: $(TEST_PREREQS) ## Run tests with race detection
	$(call TEST_RUN,go test -race -count=1 ./...)

test-integration: $(TEST_PREREQS) ## Run integration tests (in-process IMAP/SMTP)
	$(call TEST_RUN,go test -race -count=1 -tags=integration ./...)

#!/bin/sh
# Flake-hunt loop for the one-off internal/daemon FAIL seen under `make test`
# on 2026-10-23. Runs the same PATH `make test` builds (per-checkout
# beadle-email, GOPATH/bin for ethos, uv tool dir --bin for biff) so the
# MCP registry subtests actually exercise the real binaries. Keeps every
# log under the worktree's .tmp/ (never /tmp), named by run number, until
# a FAIL recurs or 40 runs complete clean.
set -u
cd <repo>/.claude/worktrees/mcp-serve || exit 1
LOGDIR=.tmp/daemon-flake-hunt
mkdir -p "$LOGDIR"
uvbin=$(uv tool dir --bin)
export PATH="$(pwd)/.tmp/bin:~/go/bin:$uvbin:$PATH"
i=1
while [ "$i" -le 40 ]; do
	log="$LOGDIR/run-$i.log"
	go test -race -count=1 ./internal/daemon/... -v > "$log" 2>&1
	status=$?
	if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
		echo "FAIL on run $i (exit $status), log: $log" >> "$LOGDIR/summary.txt"
		echo "FAIL on run $i (exit $status)"
		exit 0
	fi
	echo "run $i ok" >> "$LOGDIR/summary.txt"
	rm -f "$log"
	i=$((i + 1))
done
echo "40 clean runs, no recurrence" >> "$LOGDIR/summary.txt"
echo "40 clean runs, no recurrence"

#!/bin/sh
# Flake-hunt loop for the one-off internal/daemon FAIL seen under `make test`
# on 2026-10-23 (beadle-0m1c). Runs the same PATH `make test` builds
# (per-checkout beadle-email, GOPATH/bin for ethos, uv tool dir --bin for
# biff) so the MCP registry subtests actually exercise the real binaries.
# Keeps every log under the checkout's .tmp/ (never /tmp), named by run
# number, until a FAIL recurs or 40 runs complete clean. Restarted here
# from the main checkout after PR #280 merged (d88368e) and removed the
# original worktree mid-run (run 3 of the first attempt failed, but the
# worktree vanished before its log could be written -- no captured output
# from that run).
set -u
cd <repo> || exit 1
LOGDIR=.tmp/daemon-flake-hunt
mkdir -p "$LOGDIR"
uvbin=$(uv tool dir --bin)
export PATH="$(pwd)/.tmp/bin:~/go/bin:$uvbin:$PATH"
i=1
while [ "$i" -le 40 ]; do
	log="$LOGDIR/run-$i.log"
	go test -race -count=1 ./internal/daemon/... -v > "$log" 2>&1
	status=$?
	if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
		echo "FAIL on run $i (exit $status), log: $log" >> "$LOGDIR/summary.txt"
		echo "FAIL on run $i (exit $status)"
		exit 0
	fi
	echo "run $i ok" >> "$LOGDIR/summary.txt"
	i=$((i + 1))
done
echo "40 clean runs, no recurrence" >> "$LOGDIR/summary.txt"
echo "40 clean runs, no recurrence"
SCRIPT

cat <repo>/.tmp/daemon-flake-hunt/loop.sh | head -3

tool_input.content:
---
name: check-for-running-processes-before-worktree-remove
description: Before worktree remove at close-out, check whether a background agent or loop is still writing into that worktree; removing it destroyed the only log of an intermittent test failure
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-23, closing out beadle PR #280, I ran `git worktree remove`
on the unit worktree while a background capture loop (started minutes
earlier by the adb worker to catch an intermittent `internal/daemon`
failure, bead beadle-0m1c) was running inside it. The loop hit the
failure on its third run at that exact moment; the directory vanished
before `run-3.log` flushed, and the script's own output shows "Directory
nonexistent" immediately followed by "FAIL on run 3". The only captured
occurrence of the flake was lost to my close-out sequencing.

**Why:** the close-out procedure checks `git status --short` for
untracked files before removal, and the tree was clean because the loop
wrote under the gitignored `.tmp/`. A clean status says nothing about
processes. I had also just told the worker to start that loop, so the
information was in my own context and I did not connect it.

**How to apply:** before `git worktree remove`, ask two things, not one:
is the tree clean, and is anything I dispatched still running there.
Concretely: `ls -lt <worktree>/.tmp/` for files modified in the last
few minutes, and a mental sweep of every background agent I started on
that unit. If a loop or agent is live, either let it finish or tell the
worker to relocate it to the main checkout first. Related:
[[judge-workers-by-transcript-not-hook-files]].

# Design: resolving MCP server binaries at spawn time, not from the worker's PATH

Design for bead `beadle-tsku` (P2, found by Qodo reviewing PR #280).

## What this change alters

`WorkerSpawner.Run` (`internal/daemon/spawner.go`) sets the Claude Code
worker subprocess's `PATH` to a fixed three-entry string:

```go
workerPATH := filepath.Dir(claudePath) + ":/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin"
```

That restricted `PATH` is deliberate — the comment above it ties it to
defense against a compromised or adversarial worker reaching arbitrary
host binaries. But `DefaultMCPRegistry()` (`internal/daemon/templates.go`)
names three stdio MCP servers by bare command name — `ethos`, `beadle-email`,
`biff` — and `BuildMCPConfig` writes those bare names straight into the
per-spawn `mcp-config.json` it hands to `claude --mcp-config`. When the
worker process starts, Claude Code's MCP client resolves `"command":
"ethos"` against *the worker subprocess's own* `PATH` — the three-entry
string above — not against the daemon's `PATH`.

None of the three install locations the Makefile's provisioning targets
use are on that list:

| Binary | Provisioning target | Install location |
|---|---|---|
| `ethos` | `tools-ethos` | `go install`'s resolved `GOBIN` or first `GOPATH` entry's `bin/` (`$GOINSTALL_BIN`, Makefile L242-244) |
| `biff` | `tools-biff` | `uv tool dir --bin` (typically `~/.local/bin`, but not guaranteed) |
| `beadle-email` | `tools-beadle-email` | `$(CURDIR)/.tmp/bin` (per-checkout self-build) |

`handler.go`'s own `whitelistDirs` for the **CLI** runner already hits this
exact mismatch for a parallel case — it includes
`~/.local/bin` plus the running daemon binary's own directory, which
happens to catch `beadle-email` when the daemon is installed there, but
still misses a `go install`-provisioned `ethos` or a `uv`-provisioned
`biff` whose bin dir differs from `~/.local/bin`. The **Claude worker's**
`PATH` (`spawner.go`'s `workerPATH`) is a separate, even narrower list that
contains none of the three.

Result: every `claude` pipeline stage spawned via `ClaudeRunner.Run` starts
a worker that cannot reach its own MCP servers unless the three binaries
happen to already sit in `/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, or next to the
`claude` binary — true on no host provisioned per this repo's own
Makefile. `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal` (`templates_test.go`)
catches the registry naming a nonexistent subcommand, by invoking the
command directly from the *test process's* `PATH` (widened by `make
test`'s `TEST_RUN` to include all three provisioning targets) — it does
not catch this bug, because it never goes through `WorkerSpawner.Run`'s
narrowed `PATH` at all. The gap is between two correct-in-isolation
pieces: the registry test proves the commands exist and work; the spawner
proves the subprocess environment is restricted. Nothing proves the
restricted environment can still reach what the registry names.

## How this leaves the system better

Today, whether an MCP server is reachable from inside a worker depends on
an accident of which bin directories exist at `/usr/bin`,
`/usr/local/bin`, and next to `claude` on the specific host — i.e., on
whatever the worker's environment happens to contain, inherited un-audited
from however the daemon process itself was started. That is not a trust
boundary at all; it is incidental behavior that happens to work on a
developer's machine (where `~/.local/bin` is often already first on a
*user's* shell `PATH`, though never on the worker subprocess's,
constructed fresh in `spawner.go` rather than inherited) and silently
breaks in a minimal deployment (a systemd unit with an explicit,
minimal `Environment=` block; the provisioning targets' install
locations were never a promise about runtime `PATH` contents, only
about where `make test` can find them).

The fix moves resolution of "which binary backs this MCP server" into the
daemon's own decision, made once, explicitly, at the moment the daemon
builds each worker's `mcp-config.json` — using the daemon's *own*
environment (which the operator controls directly, e.g. via the
provisioning unit's `PATH=`) to look up each registry entry's `Command`,
and writing the resolved absolute path into the config. The worker's `PATH`
stays exactly as restricted as it is today; it is simply no longer asked
to do this resolution at all. What a worker can execute is a *daemon-made
decision, frozen into an immutable per-spawn file before the worker
starts*, not an environment variable the worker's own process can act on.
That is a tighter trust boundary than today's: today's design depends on
nobody standing between the daemon-set `PATH` string and the worker's
ability to decide — for itself, via normal `PATH` search rules — what
`ethos` resolves to, if `PATH` is ever widened for any other reason.
Fixing it at the config-write step removes that dependency entirely:
widening the worker's `PATH` tomorrow, for an unrelated reason, no longer
has any bearing on which `ethos` binary a worker's MCP client invokes.

## Approaches compared

### (A) — Resolve at config-build time, write the absolute path

`BuildMCPConfig` (or a thin wrapper `ClaudeRunner.Run` calls before it)
resolves each **selected** entry's `Command` via `exec.LookPath` run in
the *daemon's* own environment (i.e., the daemon process's inherited
`PATH`, never the worker's), and writes the resolved absolute path as
`MCPServerConfig.Command` in the per-spawn JSON. The worker's `PATH`
(`spawner.go`'s `workerPATH`) is untouched.

- **What the worker can execute.** Exactly the fixed absolute paths the
  daemon resolved at spawn time, for the fixed set of MCP servers that
  spawn's `cmd.MCPServers` named — nothing else, regardless of what the
  worker's own `PATH` contains. A worker cannot widen its own MCP-server
  surface by manipulating `PATH`, because the config no longer does a
  `PATH` search at spawn time at all; Claude Code execs the literal path
  string.
- **What a compromised worker gains.** Nothing new. A compromised worker
  already inherits whatever `cmd.MCPServers` + the registry grant it for
  that stage; this approach does not expand or contract that grant, it
  only removes the one path by which an *accidental* `PATH` change
  (widening `/usr/bin` with a symlink, say) could have altered what those
  names resolve to.
- **What happens when the binary is absent at spawn time.** `exec.LookPath`
  fails in `BuildMCPConfig`, which already returns `(string, error)` for
  exactly this family of failure (`unknown MCP server`, `cfg.Validate()`
  failure) — this is one more branch of the same function, not a new
  failure surface. `ClaudeRunner.Run` already treats a `BuildMCPConfig`
  error as fatal to the stage (`runner.go:75-78`, `return "", fmt.Errorf("build
  mcp config: %w", err)`), which the caller (`Executor.Run`, `pipeline.go`)
  already turns into `p.Error` + `fireElse` — the pipeline is marked
  failed and the sender is replied to, with no `claude` process ever
  started. This is the existing failure path for `beadle-qtei`'s declared
  env vars (`runner.go`'s `resolveEnvVars` check, same function), reused
  verbatim for a declared MCP command.
- **What the daemon logs.** One `slog` line per resolution failure, naming
  the registry entry and the unresolved `Command` — the same shape
  `e.Logger.Info("stage mission created", ...)` already uses just above
  the call site, so no new logging convention is introduced.

### (B) — Extend the worker PATH with the provisioning targets' install dirs

Add `$GOINSTALL_BIN`-equivalent and `uv tool dir --bin`-equivalent
directories to `spawner.go`'s `workerPATH` construction, alongside
`/usr/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`.

- **What the worker can execute.** Any executable in those directories,
  not only `ethos`/`biff`/`beadle-email` — `go install` and `uv tool
  install` are general-purpose install mechanisms, and either bin dir can
  (now or later) contain other tools an operator or a prior `uv tool
  install` happened to place there. The grant is "this whole directory,"
  not "this one registry entry."
- **What a compromised worker gains.** The ability to invoke anything that
  directory holds, by name, via the worker's own built-in `Bash` tool (when
  granted) or any other mechanism that shells out — a strictly larger
  surface than approach (A), which never exposes a searchable `PATH`
  directory to the worker at all, only a config file naming fixed absolute
  paths for the servers Claude Code itself spawns.
- **What happens when the binary is absent at spawn time.** Nothing
  catches it before the worker starts. The worker starts normally
  (`--bare` mode has no pre-flight MCP connectivity check), Claude Code
  attempts to connect to `ethos serve` as its first MCP use, `PATH`
  search fails, and the worker either silently runs without that MCP
  server or fails deep inside its own turn loop — exactly the
  "pipeline record created, nothing downstream actually runs" failure
  mode `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s Design Invariants section already flags as a
  known gap for a different reason (missing GPG authorization on mission
  creation). This approach adds a second way to reach that same silent
  failure shape, for an entirely mechanical cause.
- **What the daemon logs.** Nothing, by construction — the daemon never
  attempts the resolution itself, so it has nothing to log. Any diagnostic
  trail exists only inside the worker's own transcript, if the worker's
  turn gets far enough to report the connection failure at all.

### (C) — A daemon-config allowlist of absolute paths per registry entry

Add a field (e.g. `~/.punt-labs/beadle/daemon.json`'s existing `Config`
struct, per `docs/wire-verifysignature.md`'s precedent) mapping each
registry entry name to an absolute path the operator sets explicitly,
e.g. `{"mcp_binaries": {"ethos": "~[redacted-user]/go/bin/ethos", ...}}`. The
daemon reads this at startup and uses it in place of resolution.

- **What the worker can execute.** The exact paths an operator wrote into
  config — in principle the narrowest of the three, since nothing is
  derived at runtime at all.
- **What a compromised worker gains.** Nothing beyond approach (A) — the
  worker still only ever sees the resolved absolute paths in its
  `mcp-config.json`.
- **What happens when the binary is absent at spawn time.** Depends on
  whether the daemon validates the configured path's existence at startup
  (not specified by this approach alone) versus only at spawn time (same
  shape as (A)). Either way, this approach adds a **new required
  onboarding step**: `docs/wire-verifysignature.md` already documents that
  there is no `beadle init`/`sign` onboarding flow yet (tracked as
  `beadle-7gm`), so an operator today configures nothing beyond `email.json`
  to get a running daemon. This approach would make every fresh deployment
  non-functional until the operator manually populates three more config
  paths it is their job to keep in sync with wherever `make tools-*`
  happened to install things — the exact kind of configuration drift (A)
  avoids, since (A) re-derives the answer from the daemon's own `PATH` on
  every spawn.
- **What the daemon logs.** Same as (A), once the binary-presence check
  exists — but the check is now validating operator-entered config,
  which is a second source of truth to keep current, not a live read of
  the daemon's own resolved environment.

### Recommendation

**Approach (A).** It is the only one of the three that *removes* a trust
surface rather than relocating or widening it: the worker's `PATH` search
capability for the registry's binaries is eliminated entirely, replaced by
a daemon-computed, written-once, immutable-per-spawn absolute path. (B)
loses because it grants the worker a directory, not a binary — a strictly
larger surface for the same problem, and one that degrades silently
instead of failing the stage. (C) loses on convenience and staleness, not
on the trust boundary itself — it is roughly A-equivalent in what the
worker can reach, but it reintroduces exactly the kind of manual,
drift-prone configuration step `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s Design Invariants
section already singles out as an open gap (`beadle-7gm`) for an unrelated
reason, and it would be the first daemon feature whose happy path requires
hand-editing `daemon.json` before the daemon is useful at all. (A) instead
extends the pattern `runner.go`'s `resolveEnvVars` already established for
declared env vars: a declared dependency is resolved against the daemon's
own environment, at the point of use, and a resolution failure fails the
stage before any subprocess starts.

## Failure behavior

When a selected registry entry's `Command` cannot be resolved via
`exec.LookPath` in the daemon's environment, `BuildMCPConfig` returns an
error before any temp file is written, naming the registry entry and the
unresolved `Command` string. `ClaudeRunner.Run` propagates that error
immediately — **no `claude` process is ever started** for that stage.
`Executor.Run` (`pipeline.go`) treats this exactly like every other
stage-runner error already handled at that call site: it sets `p.Error`
to the wrapped message, calls `e.fireElse(p)`, which marks the pipeline
record failed and sends the configured reply to the email's sender. This
mirrors `runner.go`'s existing `resolveEnvVars` check line for line: both
are preflight checks against a declared dependency, both fail the stage
before any subprocess work happens, and both produce a pipeline record
whose `Error` field names exactly what was missing — never a worker that
starts, consumes its turn budget, and fails opaquely on first MCP use.

## Implementation write set (for the follow-up implementation mission)

- `internal/daemon/templates.go` — add the resolution step to
  `BuildMCPConfig` (or a small helper it calls), using `exec.LookPath`
  against the *process* environment (the daemon's, never a value threaded
  in from the worker side) for each selected entry whose `Command != ""`;
  leave http-shaped entries (`context7`) untouched, since `Validate()`
  already distinguishes the two shapes and only a stdio entry has a
  `Command` to resolve.
- `internal/daemon/templates_test.go` — the new test described below;
  confirm whether `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal` changes
  (see below — it does not need to, see reasoning).
- `internal/daemon/spawner.go` — update the comment above `workerPATH`
  (currently reads only as a security rationale for the restriction) to
  note that MCP server binaries no longer rely on this `PATH` at all,
  resolved instead at config-build time by `BuildMCPConfig` — so a future
  reader does not assume widening `workerPATH` is ever the right fix for
  an MCP server the worker cannot reach.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — amend the "Design Invariants" section (or the
  Package Map's `internal/daemon` row) to state the new invariant: an MCP
  server's `Command` reaching a worker's `mcp-config.json` is always an
  absolute path resolved by the daemon at spawn time, never a bare name
  the worker's own `PATH` resolves.

### The proving test

A table or single-case test in `templates_test.go`:

1. Build a scratch directory (`t.TempDir()`), write an executable fake
   binary into it (e.g. a trivial shell script, `0o755`), and set `PATH`
   to that directory only for the duration of the test
   (`t.Setenv("PATH", dir)`).
2. Call `BuildMCPConfig` with a registry containing one stdio entry whose
   `Command` matches the fake binary's name.
3. Read back the written JSON and assert the `mcpServers.<name>.command`
   field is the fake binary's **absolute** path (`filepath.Join(dir,
   name)`), not the bare name — proving resolution happened and the
   result was written, not deferred to the subprocess.
4. Remove the fake binary (or point `PATH` at an empty directory) and call
   `BuildMCPConfig` again with the same registry; assert it now returns a
   non-nil error naming the registry entry and the unresolved command —
   proving the negative case fails closed, before any file is written for
   that call, matching `resolveEnvVars`'s precedent.

**Does `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal` change?** No. That
test exercises `DefaultMCPRegistry()`'s *entries* directly against
`exec.LookPath` and `--help` in the *test process's* own `PATH` (widened by
`make test`'s `TEST_PREREQS`) — it is proving the registry's `Command`/`Args`
values name real, well-behaved binaries, a concern orthogonal to *where*
that resolution happens inside the spawn path. The new test above exercises
`BuildMCPConfig`'s resolution behavior specifically, with a synthetic
registry and a scratch `PATH` it controls — it does not touch
`DefaultMCPRegistry()` at all, so there is no reason for the existing
test's registry-correctness assertions to move or duplicate.

## Decisions for the operator

1. **Where resolution runs: approach (A), daemon-environment `PATH`
   lookup inside `BuildMCPConfig`, vs. (C), an explicit `daemon.json`
   allowlist.** Recommend (A) — it needs no new onboarding step, matches
   the `resolveEnvVars` precedent already in this codebase, and never goes
   stale relative to wherever `make tools-*` actually installed a binary.
   (C) is the fallback if the operator wants an explicit, auditable,
   hand-maintained record of exactly which binary backs each MCP server —
   a stronger supply-chain story at the cost of a new required config step
   on every fresh deployment.
2. **Whether `workerPATH`'s three-entry restriction should also drop
   `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/bin`, now that MCP resolution no longer
   needs any directory on the worker's `PATH` at all.** Out of scope for
   this bead (those two entries exist for `git` and other basic tools a
   worker's `Bash` grant may need, unrelated to MCP resolution), but worth
   a follow-up bead if the goal is to shrink the worker's reachable
   binary set further. Recommend leaving it alone here and filing that
   separately, so this PR stays scoped to the one defect Qodo found.
3. **Whether the new `BuildMCPConfig` resolution failure should also
   appear as a structured field on the pipeline record** (today, errors
   land only in the free-text `p.Error` string, per the existing pattern
   for every other stage-runner failure). Recommend no change here —
   consistent with how `resolveEnvVars`'s failure and every other
   `ClaudeRunner.Run`/`CLIRunner.Run` error already surface, and a
   structured-error redesign for pipeline failures generally is a bigger,
   separate concern than this bead.

## Draft DESIGN.md ADR entry

```markdown
## DES-037: MCP server binaries resolved at spawn time, not via worker PATH

**Decision:** `BuildMCPConfig` (`internal/daemon/templates.go`) resolves
each selected stdio MCP server's `Command` with `exec.LookPath` run in the
daemon's own environment, and writes the resolved absolute path into the
per-spawn `mcp-config.json`. The worker subprocess's restricted `PATH`
(`spawner.go`'s `workerPATH`) is unchanged and plays no role in locating
MCP server binaries.

**Why:** `DefaultMCPRegistry()` names `ethos`, `beadle-email`, and `biff`
by bare command name, relying on the worker's own `PATH` to resolve them
at MCP-connect time. The worker's `PATH` is `<claude dir>:/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin`
(`spawner.go`) — none of which matches where this repo's own provisioning
targets (`tools-ethos`, `tools-biff`, `tools-beadle-email`) install those
binaries. Every `claude`-runner pipeline stage therefore started a worker
that could not reach its own MCP servers on any correctly provisioned
host (found by Qodo on PR #280; tracked as `beadle-tsku`).

**Alternatives considered:**

- Widen `workerPATH` with the provisioning targets' install directories.
  Rejected: grants the worker an entire searchable directory rather than
  one resolved binary path, is a strictly larger reachable-execution
  surface for a compromised worker, and degrades silently (the worker
  starts, then fails deep inside its own turn loop on first MCP use)
  rather than failing the pipeline stage before any subprocess starts.
- An explicit `daemon.json` allowlist mapping registry entries to absolute
  paths. Rejected for now: adds a new required, hand-maintained onboarding
  step with no onboarding flow to carry it (`beadle-7gm` tracks the
  general gap), and goes stale independently of wherever `make tools-*`
  actually installed a binary — a maintenance cost (A) avoids by
  re-resolving from the daemon's live environment on every spawn.

**Consequences:** An MCP server binary absent from the daemon's own `PATH`
at spawn time now fails the pipeline stage immediately, with the registry
entry and command named in the pipeline's error and the sender's reply —
before any worker process starts, matching the existing preflight-failure
pattern `resolveEnvVars` established for declared env vars
(`internal/daemon/runner.go`). The worker's execution surface for MCP
server binaries is now a daemon-computed, written-once, per-spawn absolute
path rather than anything resolvable at runtime from inside the worker
process.
```

tool_input.message:
Evaluation of mission m-2026-10-22-055 (beadle-tsku, docs/worker-mcp-path.md, commit 5626265 on fix/worker-mcp-path). Verdict: the design is sound — recommend ratifying approach (A) — with one finding the doc should address before the implementation mission dispatches, plus two minor completeness notes.

**(1) Worker execution surface: approach A narrows it, confirmed against code.** Today `BuildMCPConfig` (templates.go:104-146) writes bare command names into mcp-config.json; Claude Code's MCP client resolves those against the *worker's own* restricted PATH (`spawner.go:127`, `workerPATH := filepath.Dir(claudePath)+":/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin"`) — a PATH search the worker process itself performs. Under (A), the worker never does that search: the config already holds an absolute path Claude execs literally. So (A) strictly removes a capability (PATH search for named MCP binaries) from the worker and does not add one. The doc's claim at docs/worker-mcp-path.md:101-107 is accurate.

**(2) PATH-poisoning route — real, and NOT fully addressed by the doc. This is the finding.** The doc frames (A) as "only removes a dependency," but it elides a direction-of-trust shift that the mission's own question 2 was aimed at: today the *worker's own* hardcoded three-entry PATH decides what `ethos`/`beadle-email`/`biff` resolve to inside the worker process — the daemon's PATH is irrelevant to that resolution. Under (A), the *daemon's* PATH becomes the sole arbiter of which binary the worker's MCP client ultimately execs, because the daemon now does the `exec.LookPath` and hands the worker a pre-resolved absolute path it trusts without question. If an attacker can get something ahead of the real binary on the *daemon's* PATH (a writable dir earlier in a systemd unit's `Environment=PATH=`, a stray `.local/bin` entry, a TMPDIR-adjacent trick), the daemon now hands the worker a malicious absolute path and the worker's own restricted PATH offers zero protection against that, where before it was simply the wrong binary the worker would fail to resolve at all — not a compromise, a dead end.

Is this risk new? No — and the doc should say so explicitly, citing the precedent it currently misses: `internal/daemon/mission.go:147` (`exec.Command("ethos", "mission", "create", ...)`), `internal/daemon/runner.go:95` (`exec.Command(ctx, "ethos", "mission", "close", ...)`), and `cmd/beadle-daemon/main.go:125` (`const gpgBinary = "gpg"`, fed into `exec.Command` inside `signature.go` for the owner-key-verification path that gates every signed command file) **already** resolve bare names against the daemon's own inherited PATH, with no isolation. The daemon process is already a bare-PATH trust root for its *own* privileged actions, including the one that verifies the GPG signature the zero-agent-authority invariant depends on. (A) extends that same existing trust assumption to MCP binary resolution; it does not introduce a new one.

**Fix for the doc:** add this precedent explicitly under "What a compromised worker gains" for (A), and add one sentence stating the scope boundary: the daemon's own environment (PATH included) is an operator-trusted input, out of scope for the worker-sandbox threat model, and (A) is consistent with — not novel relative to — the trust the daemon already places in its own PATH for `ethos`/`gpg` invocations. Without this, a future reader evaluating "does this widen the attack surface" has to reconstruct the precedent themselves (I had to grep three files to confirm it); the doc should carry the answer.

**(3) Fail-closed — confirmed reachable, code matches the doc.** `BuildMCPConfig` is called at runner.go:75, after `createMissionFromContract` (runner.go:62) but before `Spawner.Run` (runner.go:87) — no `claude` process starts on error. The error propagates through `ClaudeRunner.Run`'s return, into `Executor.Run`'s stage loop (pipeline.go:155-161), which sets `p.Status = "failed"`, `p.Error`, calls `e.fireElse(p)`, and returns — identical handling to every other stage-runner error at that call site, exactly as the doc claims. One pre-existing (not new) wrinkle the doc doesn't need to cover: the stage mission is already created via `createMissionFromContract` before `BuildMCPConfig` runs, so a `BuildMCPConfig` failure leaves an orphaned ethos mission with no worker ever spawned against it — but that's true of every post-mission-creation failure in this function already (spawn errors, prompt-build errors), not something this change introduces.

**(4) Rejection of (C) — sound, one-sentence answer holds.** (C) buys an explicit, auditable, operator-maintained pin of exactly which binary backs each MCP server — a supply-chain record independent of whatever happens to be first on PATH at spawn time — at the cost of a new manual config step with no onboarding flow (`beadle-7gm`) and configuration drift. The doc's "Decisions for the operator" section already captures this; it's consistent with `daemon.json`'s existing role as owner-key config (`docs/wire-verifysignature.md` precedent the doc itself cites).

**(5) Write set and proving test — sound.** `templates.go`/`templates_test.go`/`spawner.go` comment/`ARCHITECTURE.md` is the right set. The described test (`t.TempDir()` + `t.Setenv("PATH", dir)`, fake binary, assert absolute path written, then remove the binary and assert a failing `BuildMCPConfig` call) is a genuine can-fail proof and never touches the host's real PATH — confirmed against the existing `TestBuildMCPConfig` table style in templates_test.go, which this slots into cleanly. The doc's reasoning for why `TestDefaultMCPRegistry_StdioCommandsAreReal` (templates_test.go:241) doesn't need to change is correct: that test exercises `DefaultMCPRegistry()`'s entries directly via `exec.LookPath` in the *test process's* PATH, orthogonal to `BuildMCPConfig`'s resolution step.

**(6) Invariant naming — adequate but could be tighter.** The doc proposes amending ARCHITECTURE.md's Design Invariants (or the Package Map row) with a new invariant. It doesn't explicitly connect to the existing "Zero agent authority" invariant, but that's defensible: `cmd.MCPServers` (the *names* a worker gets) is part of the GPG-signed command file content already covered by that invariant; this change concerns only *how a name resolves to a binary path*, not an expansion of which names a worker can request. Worth one added sentence making that scope boundary explicit, but not a blocker.

**Bottom line:** ratify approach (A). Send the doc back to bwk for one addition — the PATH-poisoning precedent and scope-boundary sentence under finding (2) — before the implementation mission dispatches. Everything else in the design (failure behavior, write set, test plan, rejection of B and C) is correct against the actual code and needs no change.

name: ratification-is-for-forks-not-cleared-designs
description: Do not ask Jim to ratify a design the evaluator cleared and I agree with; the design gate exists for genuine forks and substantive issues, not for permission to proceed
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-23 I held the beadle-tsku implementation for about an hour
waiting for Jim to ratify a design (resolve MCP binaries in the daemon's
environment at spawn time) that the security evaluator had cleared
against the code and that I had read and agreed with. The three
"decisions" I presented had a clear recommendation each and no real
alternative in play. Jim said yes, then: "you should not be asking me
questions to which there is really no judgement required."

**Why:** the workflow's design gate says substantive issues go to the
operator; it does not say every design needs a signature. A design with
a reviewed recommendation and no competing option is not a fork. Asking
anyway costs an hour of idle time per unit and trains him to see my asks
as noise, which hides the asks that are real.

**How to apply:** after a design mission closes with the evaluator's
accept, dispatch implementation unless at least one decision is a
genuine fork: two approaches I cannot rank, a deviation from his stated
direction, a trust-model change with no precedent, or something that
commits his time or reputation. If I would bet on my own recommendation
and the reviewer agrees, that is not a question. Mention the design in
the next recap instead. Related: [[no-per-turn-needs-list]],
[[asks-short-and-clear]].

// Scratch eval test: only SELECTED entries are resolved; registry not mutated; http untouched.
func TestDJBEval_OnlySelectedResolved_NoMutation_HTTPUntouched(t *testing.T) {
	binDir := t.TempDir()
	okBin := filepath.Join(binDir, "ok-server")
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(okBin, []byte("#!/bin/sh\necho ok\n"), 0o755))
	t.Setenv("PATH", binDir)

	registry := map[string]MCPServerConfig{
		"ok":      {Command: "ok-server", Args: []string{"serve"}},
		"missing": {Command: "nonexistent-binary-xyz", Args: []string{"serve"}}, // absent, NOT selected
		"http":    {Type: "http", URL: "https://example.com/mcp"},
	}

	tmpl := &MissionTemplate{TmpDir: t.TempDir()}
	path, err := tmpl.BuildMCPConfig([]string{"ok", "http"}, registry)
	require.NoError(t, err, "build must succeed even though 'missing' entry's binary is absent, because it was not selected")
	defer os.Remove(path)

	// Registry map must be unmutated: the "missing" entry's Command must still be the bare name
	assert.Equal(t, "nonexistent-binary-xyz", registry["missing"].Command, "registry must not be mutated for entries not even selected")
	assert.Equal(t, "ok-server", registry["ok"].Command, "registry's own copy of the selected entry's Command must remain the bare name post-call")

	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	t.Logf("config: %s", data)
}

tool_input.message:
Silent-failure review of e161dce..95432ad (worker-path worktree). Nothing swallows the LookPath error; four findings, none CRITICAL. Each answer to your questions, then the findings.

ANSWERS
- Error propagation: not swallowed. templates.go:139-141 returns the wrapped error; runner.go:75-78 wraps it as "build mcp config: %w" and returns; pipeline.go (the runner.Run err block, ~150-156) sets p.Status="failed", p.Error, e.save(p), e.fireElse(p), and returns the error; handler.go:209-213 logs it at Error. The failed pipeline record carries the full chain.
- Sender's reply: fireElse (pipeline.go:387-424) runs the "reply" recipe, which per docs/pipeline-v2.md:1077-1081 is runner: claude with mcp_servers [ethos, beadle-email]. So when the missing binary is beadle-email, the else-reply goes through ClaudeRunner.Run -> BuildMCPConfig again and fails identically. The sender gets nothing, and the only trace of that second failure is a Warn at pipeline.go:422. Inherent (no mail without beadle-email), but see finding 3.
- Worker with an unresolved command: none. handler.go:203 is the only production registry (DefaultMCPRegistry, hardcoded bare names); ClaudeRunner is the only BuildMCPConfig caller; the spawner receives only the written path. Every stdio entry passes LookPath; http entries have Command=="" and are skipped correctly.
- LookPath with a separator: Go's lp_unix.go returns `file` unchanged (not absolutized) when it contains "/", after a findExecutable check against the daemon's CWD. See finding 2. The relative-PATH-entry case (PATH containing "" or "."), by contrast, fails closed: LookPath returns ErrDot as a non-nil error and templates.go:140 rejects it.
- Logger: not nil-and-discarding, but not the daemon's logger either. See finding 1.
- Negative test: TestBuildMCPConfig_ResolvesStdioCommand's second subtest (templates_test.go:737-752) asserts os.ReadDir(TmpDir) is empty after the error, so it proves no file remains, which is the observable that matters. It cannot distinguish never-written from written-then-removed, and it has one registry entry, so it does not prove the multi-entry ordering. See finding 4.
- selected built before any write: yes. The loop at templates.go:130-148 completes (every Validate and LookPath) before MarshalIndent and os.CreateTemp at ~154-158. A failure on the third entry writes nothing.

FINDINGS

1. HIGH — cmd/beadle-daemon/main.go:111-113. The diff adds MissionTemplate.Logger and a logger() fallback (templates.go:101,104-109), but the one production construction site still builds `&daemon.MissionTemplate{TmpDir: missionsTmpDir}` with no Logger. beadle-daemon never calls slog.SetDefault (only cmd/beadle-email/main.go:24 does), so the new "resolved mcp server command" Info line at templates.go:143 goes to the stdlib default handler: stderr only, in the log package's format, and never into ~/.punt-labs/beadle/logs/beadle-daemon.log, which main.go:40-48 feeds only through the explicitly constructed logger. The spawner's lines for the same spawn (spawner.go:136,170) do land in the file, since main.go:109 wires Logger: logger into WorkerSpawner. Six months from now the file shows the worker spawned but not which binary path it was handed. Fix: `templates = &daemon.MissionTemplate{TmpDir: missionsTmpDir, Logger: logger}`.

2. MEDIUM — templates.go:139-145 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:92. The doc comment (templates.go:113-115) and the new ARCHITECTURE invariant both say the written Command "is always an absolute path". The code does not enforce it: for a Command containing "/" LookPath returns the string verbatim after checking it relative to the daemon's CWD, so "bin/ethos" or "./ethos" would be written relative. Today's registry has only bare names and is not operator-configurable, so no production input reaches this, but the invariant is a prose claim with no guard. Add `if !filepath.IsAbs(resolved) { return "", fmt.Errorf("mcp server %q: resolved command %q is not absolute", name, resolved) }` after the LookPath (or reject separators in MCPServerConfig.Validate), and a test case for it. Cheap, and it makes the doc true by construction rather than by current registry contents.

3. MEDIUM — templates.go:141 error text, and runner.go:61 ordering. (a) The error reads `mcp server "beadle-email": resolve command "beadle-email": exec: "beadle-email": executable file not found in $PATH`. It does not say whose PATH or what to do. runner.go:52-55 set the house style for exactly this class of permanent deployment misconfiguration ("set them in the unit/plist that starts beadle-daemon"); match it: "...not found on the daemon's PATH; install it or add its directory to PATH in the unit/plist that starts beadle-daemon". (b) The new failure happens after createMissionFromContract at runner.go:61, so a LookPath failure leaves an open ethos mission that nothing closes or abandons; the mission ID is only in the Info line at runner.go:67 and is absent from p.Error, so the failed pipeline record cannot be traced to the orphan. BuildMCPConfig depends only on servers and registry, not the mission ID. Move the BuildMCPConfig call (lines 71-79) above createMissionFromContract, for the same reason the env-var check was moved first (the comment at runner.go:32-50 already argues this). The same ordering argument applies to the Warn at pipeline.go:422: when the reply recipe itself cannot resolve beadle-email, every pipeline will fail forever, which pipeline.go:191,196 log at Error for the sibling permanent cases; Warn understates it.

4. LOW — templates_test.go:737-752. Add a two-entry case (one resolvable fake, one absent, servers listed in that order) asserting error plus empty TmpDir. That is the only shape that proves "selected is built fully before any write" rather than "no file remains after a single-entry failure".

No findings on: the `_ =` on Close/Remove in the write-error path (pre-existing, primary error returned), the defer os.Remove at runner.go:79, or the http passthrough.
